title.zh: 卷62 李彪 高道悦
title.raw: 卷62 李彪 高道悦 Volume 62: Li Biao, Gao Daoyue

sentences.zh: 李彪 高道悅

translations.literal: Li Biao; Gao Daoyue
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao; Gao Daoyue

sentences.zh: 李彪，字道固，頓丘衞國人，高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Li Biao, styled Daogu, was a native of Dunqiu in Weiguo; the Emperor Gaozu bestowed this name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, whose courtesy name was Daogu, came from Dunqiu in Weiguo; Emperor Gaozu granted him this name.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微，少孤貧，有大志，篤學不倦。

translations.literal: His family background was humble; orphaned young and poor, he harbored great ambitions and studied with tireless devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a poor family, he lost his parents early and grew up in poverty, yet he cherished lofty aims and pursued learning without cease.

sentences.zh: 初受業於長樂監伯陽，伯陽稱美之。

translations.literal: At first he received instruction from the Director of Music Bo Yang of Changle; Bo Yang praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied under Bo Yang, Director of Music in Changle, who spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 晚與漁陽高悅、北平陽尼等將隱於名山，不果而罷。

translations.literal: Later, together with Gao Yue of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, and others, he planned to withdraw to famous mountains; the plan did not succeed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he and Gao Yue of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, and others intended to retire to famous mountains, but the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 悅兄閭，博學高才，家富典籍，彪遂於悅家手抄口誦，不暇寢食。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Lü was learned and highly talented, with a household rich in canonical texts; Biao thereupon copied by hand and recited aloud at Yue's home, with no leisure for sleep or food.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Lü was a scholar of wide learning and great talent, and his house held a rich library; Biao copied texts by hand and recited them aloud at Yue's home, scarcely pausing to eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 既而還鄉里。

translations.literal: Afterward he returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 平原王叡年將弱冠，[1]雅有志業，娶東徐州刺史博陵崔鑒女，路由冀相，聞彪名而詣之，修師友之禮，稱之於郡，遂舉孝廉，至京師館而受業焉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pingyuan, Rui, was nearing the capping age, [1] and from youth cherished purposeful resolve; he married the daughter of Cui Jian of Boling, Eastern Xuzhou Inspector, and on the road through Ji and Xiang, hearing Biao's fame, went to visit him, observed the rites between teacher and friend, praised him in the commandery, and thus he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, came to the capital to lodge with him and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Pingyuan was approaching manhood [1] and had long shown serious purpose; when he married the daughter of Cui Jian, inspector of Eastern Xuzhou, his route passed through Ji and Xiang. Hearing of Biao's reputation, he called on him, treated him with the courtesies due a teacher and friend, and commended him in the commandery. Biao was thereupon nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, came to the capital, lodged with the prince, and received instruction from him.

sentences.zh: 高閭稱之于朝貴，李沖禮之甚厚，彪深宗附。

translations.literal: Gao Lü praised him among the court nobility; Li Chong treated him with great courtesy, and Biao attached himself to him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lü praised him among the great families at court; Li Chong honored him generously, and Biao became his devoted follower.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，為中書教學博士，後假員外散騎常侍、建威將軍、衞國子，使於蕭賾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign he served as Erudite for Instruction at the Secretariat; later he was provisionally appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Establishes Might, and Heir of Weiguo, and was sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed Erudite for Instruction at the Secretariat; later he served provisionally as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Establishes Might, and heir of Weiguo, and was dispatched on a mission to Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書丞，參著作事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary of the Palace Library and participated in compilation work.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretary of the Palace Library and took part in the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 自成帝以來至于太和，崔浩、高允著述國書，編年序錄，為春秋之體，遺落時事，三無一存。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Cheng down to the Taihe era, Cui Hao and Gao Yun compiled the national history in annalistic form with chronological records in the manner of the Spring and Autumn Annals; contemporary events were lost, and not one of the three categories survived.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Cheng's reign through the Taihe era, Cui Hao and Gao Yun had compiled the national history as annals and chronicles in the manner of the Spring and Autumn Annals, but events were lost and none of the three categories of records remained.

sentences.zh: 彪與祕書令高祐始奏從遷固之體，創為紀傳表志之目焉。

translations.literal: Biao and the Director of the Palace Library Gao You first memorialized to adopt the format of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, establishing the categories of annals, biographies, tables, and treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Biao and Palace Library Director Gao You were the first to petition that the history follow the annal-biography form of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, establishing the categories of annals, biographies, tables, and treatises.

sentences.zh: 彪又表曰：

translations.literal: Biao again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Biao submitted another memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞昔之哲王，莫不亹亹孜孜，思納讜言，以康黎庶。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the sage kings of old were all diligent and untiring, thinking to receive forthright counsel so as to bring peace to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the sage kings of antiquity were all diligent and untiring, eager to receive honest counsel so that the people might prosper.

sentences.zh: 是以訪童問師，不避淵澤；

translations.literal: Therefore they sought out children and questioned teachers, not shunning deep pools and marshes;
translations.idiomatic: Hence they sought counsel from the young and questioned their teachers, not shrinking from the deepest waters;

sentences.zh: 詢謀諮善，不棄芻蕘。

translations.literal: they inquired into plans and consulted the good, not discarding the counsel of the humble.
translations.idiomatic: they sought advice and consulted the worthy, and did not reject the words of the lowly.

sentences.zh: 用能光茂實於竹素，播徽聲於金石。

translations.literal: Thus they could make their achievements flourish on bamboo and silk and spread their fine renown on metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: By this means their achievements were recorded on bamboo and silk, and their noble fame was inscribed on bronze and stone.

sentences.zh: 臣屬生有道，遇無諱之朝，敢修往式，竊揆時宜，謹冒死上封事七條。

translations.literal: Your servant was born in an age of the Way and encountered a court without taboos; I dare restore the former model, privately gauge what suits the time, and respectfully risk death to submit a sealed memorial of seven items.
translations.idiomatic: I was born in an age guided by the Way and have met a court where nothing may not be spoken; I dare follow the precedents of old, judge as best I can what the times require, and humbly risk my life to present this sealed memorial in seven sections.

sentences.zh: 狂瞽之言，伏待刑戮。

translations.literal: These rash and blind words await punishment.
translations.idiomatic: These rash words from a blind man await your punishment.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：自太和建號，踰于一紀，典刑德政，可得而言也。

translations.literal: The first says: Since the Taihe reign-title was established, more than one cycle has passed; the institutions, punishments, virtue, and government may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: The first point: Since the Taihe era began, more than twelve years have passed, and the rites, punishments, virtue, and governance may now be assessed.

sentences.zh: 立圓丘以昭孝，則百神不乏饗矣；

translations.literal: If the Round Mound is established to display filial piety, then the hundred spirits will not lack offerings;
translations.idiomatic: Establish the Round Mound to manifest filial piety, and the myriad spirits will never want for sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 舉賢才以酬諮，則多士盈朝矣；

translations.literal: if worthy talent is raised to answer consultation, then many scholars will fill the court;
translations.idiomatic: raise worthy men to answer your consultations, and the court will brim with talent;

sentences.zh: 開至誠以軌物，則朝無佞人矣；

translations.literal: if utmost sincerity is opened to guide things, then the court will have no flatterers;
translations.idiomatic: open your utmost sincerity to guide the realm, and there will be no sycophants at court;

sentences.zh: 敦六順以教人，則四門無凶人矣；

translations.literal: if the six harmonies are cultivated to teach the people, then the four gates will have no evil men;
translations.idiomatic: cultivate the six harmonies to instruct the people, and no wicked men will pass the four gates;

sentences.zh: 制冠服以明秩，則典式復彰矣；

translations.literal: if caps and robes are regulated to clarify rank, then the canonical forms will again be displayed;
translations.idiomatic: regulate caps and robes to clarify rank, and the canonical forms will shine forth again;

sentences.zh: 作雅樂以協人倫，則人神交慶矣；

translations.literal: if elegant music is composed to harmonize human relations, then men and spirits will rejoice together;
translations.idiomatic: compose elegant music to harmonize human relations, and men and spirits will celebrate together;

sentences.zh: 深慎罰以明刑，則庶獄得衷矣；

translations.literal: if punishments are deeply weighed to clarify the penal code, then the multitude of cases will obtain the mean;
translations.idiomatic: weigh punishments with care to clarify the law, and the multitude of legal cases will be judged aright;

sentences.zh: 薄服味以示約，則儉德光昭矣；

translations.literal: if garments and food are kept plain to show restraint, then the virtue of frugality will shine;
translations.idiomatic: keep food and dress plain to show restraint, and the virtue of frugality will be manifest;

sentences.zh: 單宮女以配鰥，則人無怨曠矣；

translations.literal: if palace women are released to match widowers, then the people will have no resentment at being unmarried;
translations.idiomatic: release palace women to wed widowers, and the people will not lament lonely beds;

sentences.zh: 傾府藏以賑錫，則大賚周渥矣；

translations.literal: if the treasury is poured out to grant relief, then great bounty will be universally generous;
translations.idiomatic: pour out the treasury to grant relief, and great bounty will reach all;

sentences.zh: 省賦役以育人，則編戶巷歌矣；

translations.literal: if levies and corvée are reduced to nurture the people, then registered households will sing in the lanes;
translations.idiomatic: reduce taxes and corvée to nurture the people, and households throughout the realm will sing in the lanes;

sentences.zh: 宣德澤以懷遠邇，則華荒抃舞矣；

translations.literal: if virtue and favor are proclaimed to embrace near and far, then the civilized and the wild will clap and dance;
translations.idiomatic: proclaim virtue and grace to embrace near and far, and the civilized and the barbarian will dance for joy;

sentences.zh: 垂至德以暢幽顯，則禎瑞效質矣。

translations.literal: if supreme virtue is extended to penetrate the hidden and the manifest, then auspicious omens will present their substance.
translations.idiomatic: extend supreme virtue to the hidden and the manifest, and auspicious omens will show their true form.

sentences.zh: 生生得所，事事惟新，巍巍乎猶造物之曲成也。

translations.literal: The living each obtain their place; every affair is made new; majestic—it is as if the Creator had brought it to completion.
translations.idiomatic: The living each have their proper place; every affair is renewed; the grandeur is as though the Creator himself had perfected the work.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚以為行儉之道，猶自闕如。

translations.literal: Yet your servant is foolish and considers that the way of practicing frugality still has gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am convinced that the practice of frugality still falls short.

translations.literal: [2] Why?
translations.idiomatic: [2] Why is this?

sentences.zh: 今四人豪富之家，習華既深，敦樸情淺，未識儉素之易長，[3]而行奢靡之難久。

translations.literal: Now the four classes of wealthy and powerful families, having long been steeped in splendor, are shallow in plain sincerity and do not know how easily frugality may be sustained, [3] yet how hard extravagance is to maintain.
translations.idiomatic: Today the wealthy and powerful of the four ranks, long accustomed to luxury, are shallow in plain sincerity; they do not see how easily thrift can be sustained [3], nor how hard extravagance is to keep up.

sentences.zh: 壯制第宅，美飾車馬，僕妾衣綾綺，土木被文繡，僭度違衷者眾矣。

translations.literal: They build mansions on a grand scale, beautifully adorn carriages and horses, dress servants and concubines in silk brocades, cover timber and earthwork with patterned embroidery—those who overstep measure and violate the mean are many.
translations.idiomatic: They build palatial residences, lavishly ornament carriages and horses, clothe servants and concubines in brocade silk, and drape timber and plaster in embroidered patterns—transgressors of rank and propriety are legion.

sentences.zh: 古先哲王之為制也，自天子以至公卿，下及抱關擊柝，其宮室車服各有差品，小不得踰大，賤不得踰貴。

translations.literal: When the sage kings of old made their institutions, from the Son of Heaven down to the public ministers, and below to the gatekeepers and night watchmen, palaces, dwellings, carriages, and dress each had its graded measure; the small could not exceed the great, nor the base the noble.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage kings of antiquity established their regulations, from the Son of Heaven down through the ministers to the gatekeepers who barred the doors and beat the night watches, dwellings, carriages, and apparel each had its proper grade; the humble could not surpass the exalted, nor the low the high.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故上下序而人志定。

translations.literal: When it is so, then superior and inferior are ordered and men's wills are settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus are high and low set in order and men's minds made firm.

sentences.zh: 今時浮華相競，情無常守，大為消功之物，巨制費力之事，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: Now the age competes in empty show; feelings have no constant hold; great are the things that waste labor, and huge are the affairs that squander strength—is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: Today men vie in empty display; constancy is gone; they lavish effort on things that waste labor and undertake projects that squander strength—is this not folly?

sentences.zh: 消功者，錦繡彫文是也；

translations.literal: What wastes labor: brocades and carved ornament;
translations.idiomatic: What wastes labor: brocades and carved ornament;

sentences.zh: 費力者，廣宅高宇、壯制麗飾是也。

translations.literal: what squanders strength: broad dwellings and high halls, grand construction and gorgeous adornment.
translations.idiomatic: what squanders strength: vast houses and towering halls, grand building and gorgeous decoration.

sentences.zh: 其妨男業、害女工者，焉可勝言哉！

translations.literal: How can one fully speak of what hinders men's work and harms women's industry!
translations.idiomatic: As for what hinders men's farming and harms women's weaving—who could recount it all!

sentences.zh: 漢文時，賈誼上疏云「今之王政可為長太息者六」，此即是其一也。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wen of Han, Jia Yi submitted a memorial saying, 'Of the present kingly government there are six matters for which one may sigh deeply'—this is one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han, Jia Yi submitted a memorial saying that the present royal government offered six matters for deep lament—and this was one of them.

sentences.zh: 夫上之所好，下必從之。

translations.literal: What those above love, those below are sure to follow.
translations.idiomatic: What the ruler loves, his subjects will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 故越王好勇而士多輕死，楚靈好瘠而國有飢人。

translations.literal: Therefore the King of Yue loved valor and his men were many who lightly faced death; King Ling of Chu loved slimness and the state had starving men.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Yue loved valor, and his warriors readily faced death; King Ling of Chu loved slender figures, and his realm had men who starved themselves.

sentences.zh: 今二聖躬行儉素，詔令殷勤，而百姓之奢猶未革者，豈楚越之人易變如彼，大魏之士難化如此？

translations.literal: Now the Two Sages personally practice frugality and plainness, and edicts are earnest, yet the people's extravagance is still not reformed—are the men of Chu and Yue so easy to change as that, and the gentlemen of Great Wei so hard to transform as this?
translations.idiomatic: Today both sage rulers personally practice thrift, and their edicts are earnest—yet the people's extravagance is not reformed. Are the people of Chu and Yue so easily changed, and the subjects of Great Wei so stubborn?

sentences.zh: 蓋朝制弗宣，人未見德，使之然耳。

translations.literal: It is simply that court regulations are not proclaimed and the people have not seen the virtue—this makes them so.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it is because court regulations have not been made clear and the people have not seen the virtue in action—that is what makes them so.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為第宅車服，自百官以至于庶人，宜為其等制，使貴不逼賤，卑不僭高，不可以稱其侈意，用違經典。

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and considers that dwellings, carriages, and dress, from the hundred officials down to the common people, should be given graded regulations, so that the noble do not press the base, the humble do not overstep the high, and none may indulge extravagant intent in violation of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that dwellings, carriages, and dress—from officials down to commoners—should be governed by graded regulations, so that the exalted do not overwhelm the humble, the low do not overstep the high, and none may indulge extravagance in defiance of the canon.

sentences.zh: 今或者以為習俗日久，不可卒革，臣謹言古人革之之漸。

translations.literal: Now some may think that custom has been long established and cannot be suddenly reformed; your servant respectfully sets forth how the ancients reformed it gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Some may say that custom is too deeply rooted to be changed at once; I respectfully explain how the ancients reformed it by degrees.

sentences.zh: 昔子產為政一年，百姓歌之曰：「我有田疇，子產伍之，我有衣冠，子產貯之，孰殺子產，吾其與之。

translations.literal: In former times, when Zichan governed, after one year the people sang: 'I have fields—Zichan has ranked them; I have robes and caps—Zichan has stored them; who kills Zichan, I will join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zichan first took office in Zheng, after one year the people sang: 'I have fields—Zichan has measured them; I have clothes—Zichan has taxed them; who kills Zichan, I will help them.'

sentences.zh: 」及三年，乃改歌曰：「我有田疇，子產殖之，我有子弟，子產誨之，子產若死，其誰繼之？

translations.literal: ' After three years they changed the song: 'I have fields—Zichan has enriched them; I have sons and younger brothers—Zichan has instructed them; if Zichan should die, who will succeed him?
translations.idiomatic: After three years they sang instead: 'I have fields—Zichan has made them fertile; I have sons—Zichan has taught them; if Zichan dies, who will follow him?'

sentences.zh: 」然則鄭人之智，豈前昏而後明哉？

translations.literal: ' Then were the people of Zheng wise—were they muddled before and clear after?
translations.idiomatic: Were the people of Zheng foolish before and wise after?

sentences.zh: 且從政者須漸，受化者難頓故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who govern must proceed gradually; those who receive transformation cannot be suddenly changed—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Those who govern must act gradually; those who are transformed cannot change all at once—that is why.

sentences.zh: 今若為制以差品之，始末之情，魏士與鄭人同矣。

translations.literal: If regulations are now made to grade them by rank, the beginning and end of the matter—the gentlemen of Wei are the same as the people of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: If regulations are now established to grade ranks, the beginning and end of the affair will show that the gentlemen of Wei are no different from the people of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 既同鄭人，是為卒有善歌，豈可憚其初怨而不為終善哉？

translations.literal: Since they are the same as the people of Zheng, in the end there will be songs of praise—how can one fear their first resentment and not achieve final good?
translations.idiomatic: Being like the people of Zheng, they will in the end sing praise—how can one fear their first resentment and refuse to seek the good that comes at last?

sentences.zh: 夫尚儉者開福之源，好奢者起貧之兆。

translations.literal: Those who esteem frugality open the source of blessing; those who love extravagance raise the omen of poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Those who honor thrift open the fountain of blessing; those who love luxury sow the seeds of want.

sentences.zh: 然則儉約易以教行，華靡難以財滿，是以聖人留意焉，賢人希準焉。

translations.literal: Thus frugality and restraint are easy to teach and practice; splendor and extravagance are hard to fill with wealth—therefore the sages took note of it, and worthy men sought to match it.
translations.idiomatic: Frugality is easy to teach and to practice; luxury is hard to sustain with wealth—therefore sages took heed of it, and worthy men strove to emulate it.

sentences.zh: 故夏禹卑宮室而惡衣服，殷湯寢黃屋而乘輅輿。

translations.literal: Therefore Yu of Xia made his palaces low and disliked fine clothes; Tang of Yin slept in a thatched hall and rode in a plain carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia built low palaces and wore coarse garments; Tang of Yin slept beneath a thatched roof and rode in an unadorned carriage.

sentences.zh: 此示儉於後王，後王所宜觀其意而取折衷也。

translations.literal: This displayed frugality to later kings; later kings should observe their intent and take the mean.
translations.idiomatic: They showed frugality to kings who came after; later kings should read their intent and strike the proper balance.

sentences.zh: 孔子為魯司寇，乘柴車而駕駑馬；

translations.literal: Confucius as Minister of Crime of Lu rode in a firewood cart and drove tired horses;
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, as Minister of Crime in Lu, rode in a cart of firewood and drove worn-out horses;

sentences.zh: 晏嬰為齊正卿，冠濯冠而衣故裘。

translations.literal: Yan Ying as Chief Minister of Qi wore a rinsed cap and old fur coat.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying, as chief minister of Qi, wore a cap he had washed again and an old fur robe.

sentences.zh: 此示儉於後臣，後臣所宜識其情而消息之也。

translations.literal: This displayed frugality to later ministers; later ministers should recognize their feeling and adjust accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: They showed frugality to ministers who came after; later ministers should understand their spirit and act accordingly.

sentences.zh: 前志云：「作法於涼，其弊猶貪。

translations.literal: A former record says: 'Making law in a cool age, its harm is still greed.
translations.idiomatic: An old text says: 'Establish law in an age of leniency, and the harm will still be greed.'

sentences.zh: 」此言雖略，有達治道。

translations.literal: ' Though this saying is brief, it penetrates the way of good government.
translations.idiomatic: Though brief, these words grasp the way of good government.

sentences.zh: 臣之瞽言，儻或可採，比及三年，可以有成。

translations.literal: Your servant's blind words may perhaps be adopted; by the time three years have passed, there may be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: My blind words may perhaps be heeded; within three years there may be results.

sentences.zh: 有成則人務本，人務本則奢費除，奢費除則穀帛豐，穀帛豐則人逸樂，人逸樂則皇基固矣。

translations.literal: If there is achievement, then the people will attend to fundamentals; if the people attend to fundamentals, then extravagant expenditure is removed; if extravagant expenditure is removed, then grain and silk are abundant; if grain and silk are abundant, then the people are at ease and joyful; if the people are at ease and joyful, then the imperial foundation is secure.
translations.idiomatic: With achievement the people will turn to fundamentals; when they turn to fundamentals, extravagance ceases; when extravagance ceases, grain and cloth abound; when grain and cloth abound, the people rest in contentment; when they rest in contentment, the imperial foundation is secure.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：易稱：「主器者，莫若長子。

translations.literal: The second says: The Changes states: 'He who holds the vessel—none is better than the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The second point: The Book of Changes says: 'He who holds the sacred vessel—none is fitter than the eldest son.'

sentences.zh: 」傳曰：「太子奉冢嫡之粢盛。

translations.literal: ' The Documents state: 'The heir apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the eldest line.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'The heir apparent presents the sacrificial grain of the direct line.'

sentences.zh: 」然則祭亡主則宗廟無所饗，冢嫡廢則神器無所傳。

translations.literal: ' Thus if sacrifice lacks a lord, the ancestral temple has nothing to receive; if the heir of the direct line is deposed, the sacred vessel has nowhere to pass.
translations.idiomatic: If sacrifice has no lord, the ancestral temple has no one to receive offerings; if the heir of the direct line is cast aside, the sacred vessel has no one to inherit it.

sentences.zh: 聖賢知其如此，故垂誥以為長世之法。

translations.literal: The sages and worthies knew it was so, and therefore left instructions to serve as the law for lasting generations.
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew this, and therefore left instructions as the law for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 昔姬王得斯道也，故恢崇儒術以訓世嫡，世嫡於是乎習成懿德，用大協於黎蒸，是以世統生人，載祀八百。

translations.literal: In former times the kings of Ji obtained this Way; therefore they broadly honored Confucian learning to instruct the heirs of the age; the heirs of the age thereupon formed accomplished virtue, and with great harmony brought peace to the multitude—thus the line continued among men and bore sacrifice for eight hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou kings grasped this Way; they exalted Confucian learning to train each generation's heir, who thereby formed virtuous character and harmonized the people—so their line endured and sacrifice continued for eight hundred years.

sentences.zh: 逮嬴氏之君於秦也，殆棄德政，坑焚儒典，弗以義方教厥冢子，於是習成凶德，肆虐以臨黔首，是以饗年不永，二世而亡。

translations.literal: When the lords of the Ying clan ruled Qin, they nearly abandoned virtuous government, buried and burned the Confucian classics, and did not teach their heirs with the righteous method; the heirs thereupon formed vicious character and wantonly oppressed the black-headed people—thus their sacrificial years were not long, and they perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ying clan ruled Qin they nearly cast aside virtuous rule, entombed and burned the Confucian canon, and did not teach their heirs by righteous example; the heirs formed vicious character and tyrannized the people—so their dynasty was brief and ended in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 亡之與興，其道在於師傅，師傅之損益，可得而言。

translations.literal: Whether a state perishes or rises, the Way lies in the tutor; the gain or loss from tutors may be spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a realm falls or flourishes depends on the tutor; what tutors add or subtract can be plainly seen.

sentences.zh: 益者，周公傅成王，教以孝仁禮義，逐去邪人，不使見惡人，選天下之端士、孝悌博聞有道術者以為衞翼。

translations.literal: What adds: the Duke of Zhou tutored King Cheng, teaching filial piety, benevolence, rites, and righteousness, driving away evil men and not letting him see wicked men, selecting the most upright gentlemen of the realm—filial, fraternal, broadly learned, and possessed of the Way and arts—to serve as his guard and wings.
translations.idiomatic: What adds: the Duke of Zhou tutored King Cheng, teaching filial piety, benevolence, ritual, and righteousness; he drove away evil men and kept the king from seeing the wicked; he chose the most upright men in the realm—filial, learned, and possessed of the Way—to guard and assist him.

sentences.zh: 衞翼良，成王正，周道之所以長久也。

translations.literal: When guard and wings are good, King Cheng is upright—this is why the Zhou Way endured long.
translations.idiomatic: With good guardians, King Cheng was upright—that is why the Zhou endured.

sentences.zh: 損者，趙高傅胡亥，教以刑戮斬劓及夷人族，逐去正人，不得見善士，諂佞讒賊者為其左右。

translations.literal: What subtracts: Zhao Gao tutored Hu Hai, teaching execution, mutilation, and extermination of clans, driving away upright men and not letting him see good gentlemen, with flatterers and slanderous villains as his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: What subtracts: Zhao Gao tutored Hu Hai, teaching execution, mutilation, and the wiping out of families; he drove away upright men and kept Hu Hai from seeing the good; flatterers and slanderers stood at his side.

sentences.zh: 左右邪，胡亥僻，秦祚之所以短促也。

translations.literal: When attendants are evil, Hu Hai is perverse—this is why the Qin fortune was brief.
translations.idiomatic: With evil attendants, Hu Hai grew crooked—that is why Qin's fortune was short.

sentences.zh: 夫皇天，輔德者也，豈私周而疏秦哉？

translations.literal: Heaven assists virtue—did it favor Zhou and slight Qin?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven assists the virtuous—did it favor Zhou and slight Qin?

sentences.zh: 由所行之道殊，故禍福之途異耳。

translations.literal: Because the ways they walked differed, the paths of fortune and calamity were different.
translations.idiomatic: Because the paths they walked differed, their roads to blessing and disaster diverged.

sentences.zh: 昔光武議為太子置傅，以問其羣臣，羣臣望意，皆言太子舅執金吾、新陽侯陰就可。

translations.literal: In former times Guangwu deliberated on appointing a tutor for the heir apparent and asked his ministers; the ministers read his intent and all said the heir's uncle, Bearer of the Golden Mace, Marquis Xin of Yang, Yin Jiu, would do.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu of Han considered appointing a tutor for the heir apparent, he asked his ministers; reading his wish, they all named the heir's uncle Yin Jiu, Bearer of the Golden Mace and Marquis of Xin.

sentences.zh: 博士張佚正色曰：「今立太子為陰氏乎？

translations.literal: Erudite Zhang Yi said with a stern countenance: 'Do you establish the heir for the Yin clan?
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Yi said sternly: 'Are you establishing the heir for the Yin family?

sentences.zh: 為天下乎？

translations.literal: Or for the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Or for the realm?'

sentences.zh: 即為陰氏，則陰侯可；

translations.literal: If for the Yin clan, then the Marquis of Yin will do;
translations.idiomatic: If for the Yin clan, the Marquis of Yin will suffice;

sentences.zh: 為天下，則固宜用天下之賢才。

translations.literal: if for the realm, then one should certainly use the worthy talent of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: if for the realm, you should use the worthiest talent in the realm.

sentences.zh: 」光武稱善，曰：「置傅，以輔太子也。

translations.literal: ' Guangwu praised him, saying: 'To set a tutor is to assist the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu praised him, saying: 'To appoint a tutor is to assist the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 今博士不難正朕，況太子乎？

translations.literal: If an erudite does not fear to correct me, how much more the heir apparent?
translations.idiomatic: If an erudite does not fear to correct me, how much more should he correct the heir!

sentences.zh: 」即拜佚為太子太傅，漢明卒為賢主。

translations.literal: ' He thereupon appointed Yi as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Emperor Ming of Han in the end became an excellent ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He at once appointed Yi Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Emperor Ming of Han in the end became an excellent ruler.

sentences.zh: 然則佚之傅漢明，非迺生之漸也，尚或有稱，而況迺生訓之以正道，其為益也固以大矣。

translations.literal: Thus Yi's tutoring of Emperor Ming was not instruction from birth, yet there was still praise—how much more if from birth he had been trained in the correct Way; the benefit would certainly be great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi tutored Emperor Ming only after his birth, yet even so won praise—how much greater the benefit if the heir were trained in the right Way from the cradle.

sentences.zh: 故禮曰「太子生，因舉以禮，使士負之，有司齊肅端冕，見于南郊」，明冢嫡之重，見乎天也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Rites say: 'When the heir apparent is born, he is lifted according to ritual, a gentleman carries him, the officials are reverent in caps and robes, and he is presented at the southern suburb'—showing the weight of the heir of the direct line and his presentation to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: 'When the heir apparent is born, he is raised according to ritual, a gentleman carries him, officials don formal caps and robes, and he is presented at the southern suburb'—showing the weight of the direct heir and his presentation to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 「過闕則下，過廟則趨」，明孝敬之道也。

translations.literal: 'When passing the palace gate he dismounts; when passing the temple he quickens his step'—showing the way of filial respect.
translations.idiomatic: 'When he passes the palace gate he dismounts; when he passes the temple he quickens his step'—showing the way of filial reverence.

sentences.zh: 然古之太子，「自為赤子，而教固以行矣」。

translations.literal: Yet the heir apparents of old, 'from being a newborn infant, instruction was already in practice.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown princes of old were taught from infancy: 'From the moment he is a newborn, instruction is already at work.'

sentences.zh: 此則遠世之鏡也。

translations.literal: This is the mirror of a distant age.
translations.idiomatic: This is the mirror of distant ages.

sentences.zh: 高宗文成皇帝慨少時師不勤教，嘗謂羣臣曰：「朕始學之日，年尚幼沖，情未能專，既臨萬機，不遑溫習，今而思之，豈唯予咎，抑亦師傅之不勤。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong, the Cultured Emperor, lamented that in youth his teachers did not instruct diligently; he once told his ministers: 'When I first studied, I was still young and my mind could not concentrate; once I faced the myriad affairs of state, I had no leisure to warm over my studies; thinking of it now, is it only my fault? It is also that my tutors were not diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong, the Cultured Emperor, lamented that in youth his teachers had not instructed him diligently. He once told his ministers: 'When I first began to study I was still young and could not concentrate; once I assumed the myriad affairs of state I had no leisure to review my lessons. Looking back, is the fault mine alone? My tutors too were not diligent.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書李訢免冠而謝，此則近日之可鑒也。

translations.literal: ' Minister of Works Li Xin removed his cap and apologized—this is what may serve as a recent mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Xin removed his cap and apologized—this is a mirror of recent times.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太皇太后翼贊高宗，訓成顯祖，使巍巍之功邈乎前王。

translations.literal: I bow before the Grand Empress Dowager, who assisted Gaozong and instructed the Manifest Ancestor, making lofty achievements surpass the kings of old.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before the Grand Empress Dowager, who assisted Emperor Gaozong and trained the Manifest Ancestor, raising achievements that surpass the kings of old.

sentences.zh: 陛下幼蒙鞠誨，聖敬之躋，及儲宮誕育，復親撫誥，日省月課，實勞神慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty from youth received nurturing instruction, and sacred reverence has ascended; when the heir's palace was born, you again personally instructed, examining day by day and reviewing month by month—truly this has taxed your divine thought.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty from childhood received nurturing instruction, and sacred reverence has grown; when the heir was born you again personally taught him, reviewing day by day and month by month—truly this has taxed your spirit.

sentences.zh: 今誠宜準古立師傅以訓導太子，訓導正則太子正，太子正則皇家慶，皇家慶則人幸甚矣。

translations.literal: Now it is truly fitting to follow antiquity in establishing tutor and assistant to instruct and guide the heir apparent; if instruction is correct then the heir is correct, if the heir is correct then the imperial house is blessed, and if the imperial house is blessed then the people are exceedingly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should truly follow antiquity and establish tutors to instruct the heir apparent; if instruction is correct the heir will be correct, if the heir is correct the imperial house will prosper, and if the imperial house prospers the people will be blessed beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 其三曰：臣聞國本黎元，人資粒食，是以昔之哲王莫不勤勸稼穡，盈畜倉廩。

translations.literal: The third says: Your servant has heard that the state's foundation is the black-headed people, and men rely on grain for food; therefore the sage kings of old were all diligent in encouraging agriculture and filling the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The third point: I have heard that the foundation of the state is the common people, who live by grain; therefore the sage kings of old all diligently encouraged farming and filled the storehouses.

sentences.zh: 故堯湯水旱，人無菜色者，蓋由備之有漸，積之有素。

translations.literal: Therefore when Yao and Tang faced flood and drought, the people had no sign of hunger on their faces—this was because preparation had been gradual and accumulation long-standing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao and Tang suffered flood and drought, the people did not go hungry—because stores had been built up gradually over time.

sentences.zh: 暨于漢家，以人食少，乃設常平以給之；

translations.literal: Reaching the Han house, because human food was scarce, they established Ever-Normal Granaries to supply it;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, because food was scarce, Ever-Normal Granaries were established to supply the people;

sentences.zh: 魏氏以兵糧乏，制屯田以供之。

translations.literal: the Wei clan, because military grain was lacking, instituted tuntian fields to provide it.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei, because military grain ran short, instituted colony fields to supply the armies.

sentences.zh: 用能不匱當時，軍國取濟。

translations.literal: By this means they were not depleted in their time, and army and state obtained relief.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they did not want in their own day, and both army and state were sustained.

sentences.zh: 又記云：國無三年之儲，謂國非其國。

translations.literal: A record also says: A state without three years' stores is called a state that is not a state.
translations.idiomatic: A classic also says: A state without three years' reserves is not truly a state.

sentences.zh: 光武以一畝不實，罪及牧守。

translations.literal: Guangwu punished prefects and governors because one mu did not bear fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu held prefects and governors guilty when a single mu failed to yield.

sentences.zh: 聖人之憂世重穀，殷勤如彼；

translations.literal: The sages' care for the age and weight on grain were as earnest as that;
translations.idiomatic: The sages' concern for the world and emphasis on grain were as earnest as that;

sentences.zh: 明君之恤人勸農，相切若此。

translations.literal: enlightened rulers' compassion for the people and encouragement of farming were as pressing as this.
translations.idiomatic: enlightened rulers' care for the people and urging of agriculture were as urgent as this.

sentences.zh: 頃年山東饑，去歲京師儉，內外人庶出入就豐，既廢營產，疲而乃達，又於國體實有虛損。

translations.literal: In recent years Shandong suffered famine; last year the capital was lean; inner and outer people went back and forth seeking abundance, abandoning their livelihoods, exhausted before they arrived—and this truly entailed a hollow loss to the body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Shandong has known famine; last year the capital was straitened; people within and without traveled far seeking grain, abandoning their trades and arriving only in exhaustion—an empty loss to the state itself.

sentences.zh: 若先多積穀，安而給之，豈有驅督老弱餬口千里之外？

translations.literal: If grain had first been accumulated in abundance and supplied in peace, how could there have been driving and supervision of the old and weak to fill their mouths a thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: Had grain been stored abundantly beforehand and distributed calmly, who would have driven the old and weak a thousand li away merely to eat?

sentences.zh: 以今況古，誠可懼也。

translations.literal: Comparing the present with antiquity, it is truly fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against antiquity, the present situation is truly alarming.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜析州郡常調九分之二，京都度支歲用之餘，各立官司，年豐糴積於倉，時儉則加私之二，[4]糶之於人。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it fitting to divide two-ninths of the regular levies of provinces and commanderies, and from the capital's annual surplus of expenditures, each establish offices; in years of abundance buy grain and store it in granaries, and in lean years add two-tenths to private [4] and sell grain to the people.
translations.idiomatic: I believe two-ninths of the regular levies of provinces and commanderies, together with the capital's annual surplus, should fund separate offices: in good years grain should be bought and stored; in lean years an extra two-tenths [4] should be added and grain sold to the people.

sentences.zh: 如此，民必力田以買官絹，又務貯財以取官粟，年登則常積，歲凶則直給。

translations.literal: Thus the people will surely labor in the fields to buy official silk, and also strive to store wealth to obtain official grain; in prosperous years there will be regular accumulation, in famine years direct supply.
translations.idiomatic: Then the people will work the fields to buy official silk and save to buy official grain; in good years stores will grow, in bad years grain will be issued directly.

sentences.zh: 又別立農官，取州郡戶十分之一以為屯民，[5]相水陸之宜，料頃畝之數，以贓贖雜物餘財市牛科給，令其肆力。

translations.literal: Further, separately establish agricultural officials, take one-tenth of households in provinces and commanderies as colony people, [5] consider suitability of water and land, calculate the number of mu, use fines and miscellaneous surplus property to buy oxen and allot them by statute, and order them to exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Further, establish agricultural officials, take one-tenth of households in each province and commandery as colony farmers [5], suit water and land, calculate acreage, use redemption fines and surplus goods to buy oxen and allot them by rule, and set them to work.

sentences.zh: 一夫之田，歲責六十斛，蠲其正課并征戍雜役。

translations.literal: One man's field: yearly obligation sixty hu; exempt his regular tax and corvée including frontier service and miscellaneous duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each man's holding should yield sixty hu per year; regular tax, frontier duty, and miscellaneous corvée should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 行此二事，數年之中，則穀積而人足，雖災不為害。

translations.literal: If these two measures are carried out, within several years grain will accumulate and the people will be sufficient; even disaster will not harm.
translations.idiomatic: Carry out these two measures and within a few years grain will accumulate and the people will be secure; even disaster will not undo them.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞前代明主，皆務懷遠人，禮賢引滯。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that enlightened rulers of former ages all strove to embrace distant men and treat worthies with ritual, drawing forth the stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that enlightened rulers of old all embraced distant subjects, honored the worthy, and drew forth the neglected.

sentences.zh: 故漢高過趙，求樂毅之胄；

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Gaozu of Han, passing Zhao, sought descendants of Yue Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han, passing through Zhao, sought descendants of Yue Yi;

sentences.zh: 晉武廓定，旌吳蜀之彥。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin, when he pacified the realm, honored the eminent of Wu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin, when he pacified the realm, honored the eminent men of Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜於河表七州人中，擢其門才，引令赴闕，依中州官比，隨能序之。

translations.literal: Your servant considers it fitting in the seven provinces south of the river to select men of talent from their clans, summon them to court, and rank them according to central provinces' offices as their ability allows.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that in the seven provinces south of the river men of talent be selected from their clans, summoned to court, and ranked by central-province standards according to ability.

sentences.zh: 一可以廣聖朝均新舊之義，二可以懷江漢歸有道之情。

translations.literal: First, this can broaden the sage court's evenhanded treatment of old and new; second, it can embrace the Jiang and Han with the sentiment of returning to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: This would broaden the court's even treatment of old and new subjects, and move the Jiang and Han to return to our rule.

sentences.zh: 其四曰：昔帝舜命咎繇惟刑之恤，周公誥成王勿誤于庶獄，斯皆君臣相誡，重刑之至也。

translations.literal: The fourth says: In former times Emperor Shun charged Gao Yao to be mindful in punishments; the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng not to err in the multitude of cases—these are all ruler and minister admonishing each other, the utmost in weighting punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth point: Emperor Shun charged Gao Yao to be tender in punishments; the Duke of Zhou warned King Cheng not to err in the multitude of cases—these are ruler and minister admonishing one another, the utmost regard for criminal justice.

sentences.zh: 今二聖哀矜罪辜，小大二情，[6]讞決之日，多從降恕，時不得已，必垂惻隱，雖前王之勤聽肆赦，亦如斯而已。

translations.literal: Now the Two Sages pity the guilty, great and small alike in circumstance, [6] and on the day judgment is rendered mostly follow reduction and pardon; when they cannot avoid it, they must show compassion—though former kings diligently heard cases and granted amnesties, it is only thus.
translations.idiomatic: Today both sage rulers pity the guilty, weighing circumstances great and small [6]; on judgment day they mostly reduce sentences or pardon; when they cannot, they show compassion—former kings who diligently heard cases and granted amnesties did no more.

sentences.zh: 至若行刑犯時，愚臣竊所未安。

translations.literal: As for carrying out punishments in violation of the season, your foolish servant is privately uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: As for executing punishments out of season, I am privately uneasy.

sentences.zh: 漢制，舊斷獄報重，常盡季冬，至孝章時改盡十月，以育三微。

translations.literal: Han institutions: formerly capital cases were reported and concluded, usually by the end of winter; by the time of Emperor Xiaozhang it was changed to end by the tenth month, to nurture the three micro-seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, capital cases were formerly concluded by winter's end; under Emperor Zhang this was moved to the tenth month to nurture the three micro-seasons.

sentences.zh: 後歲旱，論者以十月斷獄，陰氣微，陽氣泄，以故致旱。

translations.literal: Later, in a year of drought, debaters held that concluding cases in the tenth month let yin qi be slight and yang qi leak, and thus caused drought.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in a drought year, critics said that concluding cases in the tenth month weakened yin and leaked yang, causing the drought.

sentences.zh: 事下公卿，尚書陳寵議：冬至陽氣始萌，故十一月有射干、芸、荔之應，周以為春；

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Three Excellencies; Minister of Works Chen Chong argued: At the winter solstice yang qi first sprouts, therefore in the eleventh month there are responses of shegan, yun, and li—the Zhou took it as spring;
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the high ministers; Chen Chong argued: at the winter solstice yang first stirs, so in the eleventh month plants sprout—the Zhou treated it as spring;

sentences.zh: 十二月陽氣上通，雉雊雞乳，殷以為春；

translations.literal: in the twelfth month yang qi penetrates upward, pheasants call and hens brood—the Yin took it as spring;
translations.idiomatic: in the twelfth month yang rises, pheasants call and hens brood—the Yin treated it as spring;

sentences.zh: 十三月陽氣已至，蟄蟲皆震，夏以為春。

translations.literal: in the thirteenth month yang qi has arrived, hibernating insects all stir—the Xia took it as spring.
translations.idiomatic: in the thirteenth month yang has arrived and insects stir—the Xia treated it as spring.

sentences.zh: 三微成著，以通三統，三統之月，斷獄流血，是不稽天意也。

translations.literal: When the three micro-seasons are manifest and clear, they penetrate the three systems; in the months of the three systems, to conclude cases and shed blood is not to accord with Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When the three micro-seasons are clear they harmonize the three systems; to execute and shed blood in those months is to disobey Heaven.

sentences.zh: 月令：仲冬之月，身欲寧，事欲靜。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances: in the mid-winter month, the body desires rest and affairs desire quiet.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say: in mid-winter the body should rest and affairs should be still.

sentences.zh: 以起隆怒，不可謂寧；

translations.literal: To rouse great anger cannot be called rest;
translations.idiomatic: To rouse great anger is not rest;

sentences.zh: 以行大刑，不可謂靜。

translations.literal: to carry out great punishments cannot be called quiet.
translations.idiomatic: to carry out great punishments is not quiet.

sentences.zh: 章帝善其言，卒以十月斷。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang approved his words and in the end concluded cases in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang approved and continued to conclude cases in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 今京都及四方斷獄報重，常竟季冬，不推三正以育三微。

translations.literal: Now in the capital and the four directions, capital cases are usually concluded by the end of winter, not extending the three correct months to nurture the three micro-seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Today in the capital and throughout the realm, capital cases usually run to winter's end, not honoring the three correct months to nurture the micro-seasons.

sentences.zh: 寬宥之情，每過於昔；

translations.literal: The sentiment of leniency surpasses the past at every turn;
translations.idiomatic: Leniency exceeds that of former times;

sentences.zh: 遵時之憲，猶或闕然。

translations.literal: yet observance of seasonal statutes is still sometimes lacking.
translations.idiomatic: yet observance of seasonal law is still sometimes lacking.

sentences.zh: 豈所謂助陽發生、垂奉微之仁也？

translations.literal: Is this what is called assisting yang to generate life and extending kindness to the micro-seasons?
translations.idiomatic: Is this truly assisting yang to generate life and extending kindness to the micro-seasons?

sentences.zh: 誠宜遠稽周典，近採漢制，天下斷獄，起自初秋，盡於孟冬，不於三統之春，行斬絞之刑。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to examine the Zhou canon from afar and adopt Han institutions from near; throughout the realm cases should begin in early autumn and end in early winter, not carrying out decapitation and strangulation in the spring of the three systems.
translations.idiomatic: You should examine the Zhou canon and adopt Han practice: capital cases should begin in early autumn and end in early winter, not executing by beheading or strangulation in the spring months of the three systems.

sentences.zh: 如此，則道協幽顯，仁垂後昆矣。

translations.literal: Thus the Way will harmonize hidden and manifest, and benevolence will extend to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Way will harmonize hidden and manifest, and benevolence will reach generations to come.

sentences.zh: 其五曰：古者，大臣有坐不廉而廢者，不謂之不廉，乃曰簠簋不飾。

translations.literal: The fifth says: In antiquity, when great ministers sat guilty of lack of integrity and were dismissed, they were not called lacking integrity but were said to have 'unadorned ritual vessels.'
translations.idiomatic: The fifth point: In antiquity, when great ministers were dismissed for lack of integrity, they were not called dishonest but said to have 'unadorned ritual vessels.'

sentences.zh: 此君之所以禮貴臣，不明言其過也。

translations.literal: This is how the ruler treats honored ministers with ritual, not plainly stating their fault.
translations.idiomatic: This is how a ruler honors his ministers with ritual without plainly stating their fault.

sentences.zh: 臣有大譴，則白冠氂纓，盤水加劍，造請室而請死，此臣之所以知罪而不敢逃刑也。

translations.literal: When a minister has great censure, he wears white cap and yak-tail tassel, basin of water with sword added, goes to the execution chamber and requests death—this is how a minister knows guilt and dares not flee punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister faces great censure, he wears white cap and yak-tail tassel, carries basin and sword, goes to the chamber and asks for death—knowing guilt and not fleeing punishment.

sentences.zh: 聖朝賓遇大臣，禮同古典。

translations.literal: The sage court treats great ministers with the same ritual as the ancient canon.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage court treats great ministers with the same ritual as antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自太和以降，有負罪當陷大辟者，多得歸第自盡。

translations.literal: From the Taihe era onward, those bearing guilt who should fall under the great execution mostly obtained return home to end themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Taihe era, ministers who should suffer capital punishment have mostly been allowed to return home and take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 遣之日，深垂隱愍，言發悽淚，百官莫不見，四海莫不聞。

translations.literal: On the day of sending them off, deep hidden pity was shown, words issuing in mournful tears—no official did not see it, no place under heaven did not hear it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day they were sent off, deep pity was shown and words came with tears—every official saw it, all under heaven heard it.

sentences.zh: 誠足以感將死之心，慰戚屬之情。

translations.literal: It truly sufficed to move the hearts of those about to die and comfort the feelings of grieving kin.
translations.idiomatic: It truly moved those about to die and comforted their kin.

sentences.zh: 然恩發至衷，未著永制，此愚臣所以敢陳末見。

translations.literal: Yet grace issued from the innermost heart and was not set down in lasting institutions—this is why your foolish servant dares present this final view.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this grace came from the heart and was not fixed in lasting law—why I dare offer this final view.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文時，人有告丞相周勃謀反者，逮繫長安獄，頓辱之與皂隸同。

translations.literal: In former times, in the time of Emperor Wen of Han, someone reported that Chancellor Zhou Bo was plotting rebellion; he was arrested and imprisoned in Chang'an, humiliated the same as clerks and runners.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han, someone reported that Chancellor Zhou Bo plotted rebellion; he was imprisoned in Chang'an and humiliated like a common clerk.

sentences.zh: 賈誼乃上書，極陳君臣之義，不宜如是。

translations.literal: Jia Yi thereupon submitted a memorial, exhaustively setting forth the meaning of ruler and minister—it should not be thus.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi submitted a memorial arguing that ruler and minister should not be treated thus.

sentences.zh: 夫貴臣者，天子為其改容而體貌之，吏人為其俯伏而敬貴之。

translations.literal: Honored ministers—the Son of Heaven alters his countenance for them and treats them with bodily courtesy; clerks and people bow prostrate for them and respect them with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Honored ministers are those for whom the Son of Heaven alters his bearing and shows bodily courtesy, whom clerks bow before and honor.

sentences.zh: 其有罪過，廢之可也，賜之死可也。

translations.literal: If they have guilt or fault, dismiss them—that is permissible; grant them death—that is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: If they have faults, dismiss them or grant them death—that is permissible.

sentences.zh: 若束縛之，輸之司寇，榜笞之，小吏詈罵之，殆非所以令眾庶見也。

translations.literal: If you bind them, deliver them to the minister of justice, flog them, and petty clerks revile them—that is scarcely what you would have the multitude witness.
translations.idiomatic: To bind them, hand them to the minister of justice, flog them, and let petty clerks revile them—that is scarcely what the multitude should witness.

sentences.zh: 及將刑也，臣則北面再拜，跪而自裁。

translations.literal: When about to execute, the minister then faces north, bows twice, kneels and cuts himself.
translations.idiomatic: When execution nears, the minister faces north, bows twice, kneels, and takes his own life.

sentences.zh: 天子曰：子大夫自有過耳，吾遇子有禮矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven says: You, grandee, have your own fault; I have treated you with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven says: You, grandee, have your own fault; I have treated you with ritual.

sentences.zh: 上不使人抑而刑之也。

translations.literal: Above, one does not have men suppress and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler does not have others restrain and punish them.

sentences.zh: 孝文深納其言，是後大臣有罪，皆自殺不受刑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen deeply accepted his words; after that, great ministers who had guilt all killed themselves and did not accept punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen deeply accepted this; thereafter guilty great ministers killed themselves rather than accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 至孝武時，稍復入獄，良由孝文行之當時，不為永制故耳。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xiaowu it gradually returned to imprisonment—largely because what Emperor Xiaowen practiced in his time was not made a lasting institution.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wu's time they were again imprisoned—because Emperor Wen's practice was not made permanent law.

sentences.zh: 伏惟聖德慈惠，豈與漢文比隆哉。

translations.literal: I bow before the sage virtue, benevolent and gracious—how could it be compared with Emperor Wen's loftiness?
translations.idiomatic: Your sage virtue is benevolent and gracious—how could it be compared with Emperor Wen's?

sentences.zh: 今天下有道，庶人不議之時，臣安可陳瞽言於朝，但恐萬世之後，繼體之主有若漢武之事焉。

translations.literal: Now the realm has the Way and common people do not discuss it; how could your servant present blind words at court—except that I fear that ten thousand generations hence, succeeding rulers may have matters like Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Today the realm is well governed and the people are silent; yet I fear that ages hence succeeding rulers may act like Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 夫道貴長久，所以樹之風聲也；

translations.literal: The Way values what is long-lasting—this is how one plants the wind's sound;
translations.idiomatic: The Way values what endures—that is how one plants reputation;

sentences.zh: 法尚不虧，所以貽厥孫謀也，焉得行恩當時，而不著長世之制乎？

translations.literal: law esteems not being impaired—this is how one bequeaths plans to descendants; how can one practice grace in the moment yet not establish institutions for long generations?
translations.idiomatic: law esteems not being broken—that is how one bequeaths counsel to descendants; how can grace be shown for a moment without lasting institutions?

sentences.zh: 其六曰：孝經稱：「父子之道天性。

translations.literal: The sixth says: The Classic of Filial Piety states: 'The way of father and son is nature's endowment.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth point: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'The way of father and son is inborn.'

sentences.zh: 」書云：「孝乎，惟孝友于兄弟。

translations.literal: ' The Documents state: 'Filial—only filial and friendly to brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: 'Be filial—be filial and brotherly.'

sentences.zh: 」二經之旨，蓋明一體而同氣，可共而不可離者也。

translations.literal: The purport of the two classics is to clarify one body and shared qi—may be together but cannot be separated.
translations.idiomatic: Both classics show one body and shared breath—joined, not to be torn apart.

sentences.zh: 及其有罪，罪不相及者，乃君上之厚恩也。

translations.literal: When they have guilt, guilt not extending to one another—that is the ruler's thick grace.
translations.idiomatic: When they are guilty, guilt does not extend to one another—that is the ruler's deep grace.

sentences.zh: 至若有懼，懼應相連者，固自然之恒理也。

translations.literal: As for when there is fear, fear that should link together—that is the constant principle of nature.
translations.idiomatic: When there is fear, fear should bind them together—that is nature's constant law.

sentences.zh: 無情之人，父兄繫獄，子弟無慘惕之容；

translations.literal: Men without feeling: father and elder brother imprisoned, sons and younger brothers show no countenance of dread;
translations.idiomatic: Men without feeling: when father or elder brother is imprisoned, sons and brothers show no dread;

sentences.zh: 子弟逃刑，父兄無愧恧之色。

translations.literal: sons and younger brothers flee punishment, fathers and elder brothers show no color of shame.
translations.idiomatic: when sons and brothers flee punishment, fathers and elder brothers show no shame.

sentences.zh: 宴安榮位，遊從自若，車馬仍華，衣冠猶飾，寧是同體共氣、分憂均戚之理也？

translations.literal: Feasting in ease and honored rank, roaming and following at will, carriages and horses still splendid, caps and robes still adorned—is this the principle of sharing one body and qi, sharing worry and equal grief?
translations.idiomatic: They feast in ease, ride splendid carriages, wear fine robes—is that sharing one body, one breath, one grief?

sentences.zh: 昔秦伯以楚人圍江，素服而示懼；

translations.literal: In former times Duke Mu of Qin, when Chu men besieged Jiang, wore plain robes to show fear;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu of Qin, when Chu besieged Jiang, wore plain robes to show fear;

sentences.zh: 宋仲子以失舉桓譚，免冠而謝罪。

translations.literal: Zhongzi of Song, having wrongly recommended Huan Tan, removed his cap and apologized for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzi of Song, having wrongly recommended Huan Tan, removed his cap and apologized.

sentences.zh: 然則子弟之於父兄，父兄之於子弟，惟其情至，豈與結盟相知者同年語其深淺哉？

translations.literal: Thus sons and younger brothers toward fathers and elder brothers, and fathers and elder brothers toward sons and younger brothers—as far as feeling reaches, how can it be spoken of in the same year as sworn friends who know one another?
translations.idiomatic: Between father and son, elder and younger, feeling runs as deep as sworn friendship cannot match.

sentences.zh: 二聖清簡風俗，孝慈是先。

translations.literal: The Two Sages have purified customs; filial piety and compassion come first.
translations.idiomatic: Both sage rulers have purified customs, putting filial piety first.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為父兄有犯，宜令子弟素服肉袒，詣闕請罪；

translations.literal: Your servant is foolish and considers that when fathers and elder brothers offend, sons and younger brothers should be ordered to wear plain robes, bare the flesh, and go to the palace gate to request punishment;
translations.idiomatic: I propose that when fathers or elder brothers offend, their sons and brothers should wear plain robes, bare the shoulder, and beg punishment at the gate;

sentences.zh: 子弟有坐，宜令父兄露板引咎，乞解所司。

translations.literal: when sons and younger brothers are guilty, fathers and elder brothers should post placards admitting fault and beg to relieve the office concerned.
translations.idiomatic: when sons and brothers are guilty, fathers and elder brothers should post confession and beg to relieve them of office.

sentences.zh: 若職任必要，不宜許者，慰勉留之。

translations.literal: If the post necessarily requires them and they should not be permitted, comfort and urge them to remain.
translations.idiomatic: If the post is essential and they cannot be released, comfort them and keep them in office.

sentences.zh: 如此，足以敦厲凡薄，使人知有所耻矣。

translations.literal: Thus it will suffice to urge and discipline the shallow multitude and make men know shame.
translations.idiomatic: This would discipline the shallow and teach men shame.

sentences.zh: 其七曰：禮云：臣有大喪，君三年不呼其門。

translations.literal: The seventh says: The Rites state: When a minister has great mourning, the ruler for three years does not call at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh point: The Rites say: When a minister has great mourning, the ruler for three years does not call at his gate.

sentences.zh: 此聖人緣情制禮，以終孝子之情者也。

translations.literal: This is the sage following feeling to make ritual, to complete the filial son's feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The sage fashioned ritual from feeling to fulfill the filial son's heart.

sentences.zh: 周季陵夷，喪禮稍亡，是以要絰即戎，素冠作刺，逮于虐秦，殆皆泯矣。

translations.literal: When the Zhou age declined, mourning ritual gradually perished; therefore hemp sash and armor together, plain cap for assassination—reaching brutal Qin, nearly all were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou declined, mourning rites faded; men wore mourning sashes into battle and plain caps to assassinate—under brutal Qin they nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 漢初，軍旅屢興，未能遵古。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, armies rose repeatedly and they could not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han armies rose repeatedly and could not follow antiquity.

sentences.zh: 至宣帝時，民當從軍屯者，遭大父母、父母死，未滿三月，皆弗徭役；

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Xuan, civilians who were to follow the army in colony service, if great-grandparents or parents died and three months had not passed, were all exempt from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan, those called to military colony service whose great-grandparents or parents had died within three months were exempt from corvée;

sentences.zh: 其朝臣喪制，未有定聞。

translations.literal: mourning institutions for court ministers had no fixed report.
translations.idiomatic: mourning rules for court ministers were not fixed.

sentences.zh: 至後漢元初中，大臣有重憂，始得去官終服。

translations.literal: By the early Later Han, great ministers with heavy grief first obtained leave from office to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: By early Later Han, great ministers with heavy grief could leave office to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 暨魏武、孫、劉之世，日尋干戈，前世禮制復廢而不行。

translations.literal: Reaching the age of Cao Wei, Sun, and Liu, day by day they sought battle; former ritual systems were again abandoned and not practiced.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of Cao Wei, Sun, and Liu, war was daily; former rites were again abandoned.

sentences.zh: 晉時，鴻臚鄭默喪親，固請終服，武帝感其孝誠，遂著令以為常。

translations.literal: In Jin times, Grand Herald Zheng Mo's parents died; he firmly requested to complete mourning; Emperor Wu was moved by his filial sincerity and thereupon issued an order making it regular.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Grand Herald Zheng Mo, his parents having died, firmly requested full mourning; Emperor Wu was moved and made it law.

sentences.zh: 聖魏之初，撥亂返正，未遑建終喪之制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of sage Wei, they swept away disorder and returned to rectitude, not yet able to establish institutions for completed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of our sage Wei, restoring order, full mourning institutions were not yet established.

sentences.zh: 今四方無虞，百姓安逸，誠是孝慈道洽，禮教興行之日也。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are without worry, the hundred surnames are at ease—truly it is the day when the way of filial compassion is harmonious and ritual teaching rises.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four quarters are secure and the people at ease—truly the day for filial piety and ritual to flourish.

sentences.zh: 然愚臣所懷，竊有未盡。

translations.literal: Yet what your foolish servant cherishes in private still has what is not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what I privately still find lacking has not been exhausted.

sentences.zh: 伏見朝臣丁父憂者，[7]假滿赴職，衣錦乘軒，從郊廟之祀，鳴玉垂緌，同節慶之醼，傷人子之道，虧天地之經。

translations.literal: I observe court ministers who mourn fathers: [7] when leave ends they take office, wear brocade and ride tall carriages, follow suburban and temple sacrifices, jade pendants and dangling tassels, join festive banquets of the same season—it wounds the son's way and impairs the canon of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: I see ministers who mourn fathers [7]: when leave ends they resume office in brocade and tall carriages, attend suburban rites and banquets—it wounds the son's way and Heaven's canon.

sentences.zh: 愚謂如有遭大父母、父母喪者，皆聽終服。

translations.literal: Your servant proposes that those who encounter mourning for great-grandparents or parents all be permitted to complete mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that all who mourn great-grandparents or parents be permitted to complete mourning.

sentences.zh: 若無其人有曠庶官者，則優旨慰喻，起令視事，但綜司出納敷奏而已，國之吉慶，一令無預。

translations.literal: If there is no such person and civilian offices are vacant, then send gracious words of comfort, summon them to oversee affairs, but only manage receipts, disbursements, and memorials; for the state's auspicious celebrations, entirely order no participation.
translations.idiomatic: If offices lack replacements, comfort them and summon them only to manage accounts and memorials; bar them from state celebrations.

sentences.zh: 其軍戎之警，墨縗從役，雖愆於禮，事所宜行也。

translations.literal: For military alarms, ink mourning and following service—though it transgresses ritual, the affair should be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: For military emergencies, ink mourning while on campaign—though it breaches ritual, necessity allows it.

sentences.zh: 如臣之言少有可採，願付有司別為條制。

translations.literal: If your servant's words have anything to adopt, I wish them entrusted to the relevant offices to make separate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: If any of my words may be adopted, let the relevant offices draft separate regulations.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽而善之，尋皆施行。

translations.literal: Gaozu reviewed and approved them; soon all were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu reviewed and approved them; soon all were implemented.

sentences.zh: 彪稍見禮遇，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: Biao gradually received courteous treatment and was promoted to General of the Central Bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Biao gradually received honor and was made General of the Central Bastion.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后崩，羣臣請高祖公除，高祖不許，與彪往復，語在禮志。

translations.literal: When the Cultured Empress Dowager died, the ministers requested that Gaozu observe public mourning; Gaozu did not permit it—he and Biao went back and forth, the words recorded in the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming died, ministers asked Gaozu to leave mourning; he refused—he and Biao debated, recorded in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曰：「歷觀古事，求能非一。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued an edict, saying: 'Reviewing affairs of antiquity, seeking ability is not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: 'Looking back through antiquity, the ways of seeking talent are many.

sentences.zh: 或承藉微蔭，著德當時；

translations.literal: Some rely on slight shade and display virtue in their time;
translations.idiomatic: Some draw on modest patronage and show virtue in their own day;

sentences.zh: 或見拔幽陋，流名後葉。

translations.literal: some are raised from obscurity and their names flow to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: some are lifted from obscurity and their fame reaches later ages.

sentences.zh: 故毛遂起賤，奮抗楚之辯，苟有才能，何必拘族也。

translations.literal: Therefore Mao Sui rose from low station and vigorously opposed Chu in debate; if there is talent and ability, why must one be bound by clan?
translations.idiomatic: Mao Sui rose from humble rank and boldly debated Chu; where there is talent, why be confined by birth?

sentences.zh: 彪雖宿非清第，本闕華資，然識性嚴聰，學博墳籍，剛辯之才，頗堪時用，兼憂吏若家，載宣朝美，若不賞庸敍績，將何以勸奬勤能？

translations.literal: Though Biao from old was not of a pure lineage and originally lacked splendid credentials, yet his nature is stern and keen, his learning broad in the canonical texts, and his talent for forceful debate quite fit for the time; he also cares for officials as for family and has proclaimed the court's excellence—if we do not reward merit and record achievement, how will we encourage diligence and ability?
translations.idiomatic: Though Biao was never of an eminent house and lacked glittering pedigree, his nature is sharp and serious, his learning deep in the classics, and his forceful eloquence well suited to the age; he treats officials like kin and has spread the court's praise—without rewarding merit, how can diligence be encouraged?

sentences.zh: 可特遷祕書令，以酬厥款。

translations.literal: He may be specially promoted to Director of the Palace Library to repay his earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be specially promoted to Director of the Palace Library in reward for his service.

sentences.zh: 」以參議律令之勤，賜帛五百匹、馬一匹、牛二頭。

translations.literal: ' For his diligence in deliberating on statutes and ordinances, he was granted five hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on statutes and ordinances he was granted five hundred bolts of silk, one horse, and two oxen.

sentences.zh: 其年，加員外散騎常侍，使於蕭賾。

translations.literal: That year he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and sent on a mission to Xiao Ze.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and sent to Xiao Ze.

sentences.zh: 賾遣其主客郎劉繪接對，并設讌樂。

translations.literal: Ze sent his Master of Guests Liu Hui to receive and answer him, and also set out feasts and music.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ze sent his Master of Guests Liu Hui to receive him and provided feasts and music.

sentences.zh: 彪辭樂。

translations.literal: Biao declined the music.
translations.idiomatic: Biao declined the music.

sentences.zh: 及坐，彪曰：「齊主既賜讌樂，以勞行人，向辭樂者，卿或未相體。

translations.literal: When seated, Biao said: 'The Qi ruler has already granted feasts and music to comfort the traveling envoy; those who earlier declined music perhaps have not yet understood you.
translations.idiomatic: When seated, Biao said: 'Your lord has granted feast and music to comfort us travelers; those who declined the music may not yet have made themselves understood.

sentences.zh: 自喪禮廢替，於茲以久，我皇孝性自天，追慕罔極，故有今者喪除之議。

translations.literal: Since mourning rites were abandoned and replaced, it has been long; our emperor's filial nature is from Heaven, his longing boundless—therefore there is today's discussion of leaving mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning rites have long been in disrepair; our emperor's filial nature is heaven-sent and his longing boundless—hence today's debate over leaving mourning.

sentences.zh: 去三月晦，朝臣始除衰裳，猶以素服從事。

translations.literal: On the last day of the third month past, court ministers first removed mourning garments, yet still attended in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the third month, ministers first removed full mourning but still served in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 裴、謝在此，固應具此，我今辭樂，想卿無怪。

translations.literal: Pei and Xie are here and should surely know this; I now decline music—do not take it amiss.
translations.idiomatic: Pei and Xie are here and should know this; I decline music—surely you understand.

sentences.zh: 」繪答言：「辭樂之事，向以不異。

translations.literal: ' Hui answered: 'The matter of declining music was never different.
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied: 'Declining music was never a disagreement between us.

sentences.zh: 請問魏朝喪禮，竟何所依？

translations.literal: May I ask: on what does Wei mourning rite rely?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, what does the Wei court rely on for mourning rite?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「高宗三年，孝文踰月，今聖上追鞠育之深恩，感慈訓之厚德，執於殷漢之間，可謂得禮之變。

translations.literal: ' Biao said: 'Emperor Gaozong observed three years, Emperor Xiaowen exceeded one month; now the sage ruler, cherishing deep the grace of nurturing and feeling the thick virtue of kind instruction, holds between Yin and Han—one may call it the ritual's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: 'Emperor Gaozong mourned three years, Emperor Xiaowen more than one month; our sage ruler, cherishing nurturing grace and kind instruction, stands between Yin and Han—a proper ritual change.

sentences.zh: 」繪復問：「若欲遵古，何為不終三年？

translations.literal: ' Hui again asked: 'If you wish to follow antiquity, why not complete three years?
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked again: 'If you wish to follow antiquity, why not complete three years?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「萬機不可久曠，故割至慕，俯從羣議。

translations.literal: ' Biao said: 'The myriad affairs cannot long be neglected; therefore he cuts the utmost longing and bows to follow the multitude's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: 'The myriad affairs of state cannot long be idle; he therefore cuts short his deepest grief and yields to the assembly's counsel.

sentences.zh: 服變不異三年，而限同一期，可謂亡禮之禮。

translations.literal: The change of dress is not different from three years, yet the limit is the same period—one may call it ritual without ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The change of dress differs from three years yet the term is the same—ritual that is not ritual.

sentences.zh: 」繪言：「汰哉叔氏！

translations.literal: ' Hui said: 'Too much, Uncle's clan!
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: 'Enough, sir!

sentences.zh: 專以禮許人。

translations.literal: You specialize in using ritual to grant favors.
translations.idiomatic: You use ritual only to grant favors.

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「聖朝自為曠代之制，何關許人。

translations.literal: ' Biao said: 'The sage court itself makes institutions for an age apart—what has it to do with granting favors?
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: 'Our sage court makes institutions for an age apart—what has that to do with granting favors?

sentences.zh: 」繪言：「百官總己聽於冢宰，萬機何慮於曠？

translations.literal: ' Hui said: 'The hundred officials entrust themselves to the heir of the lineage who hears all affairs—why worry about neglect?
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: 'All officials entrust affairs to the heir who governs—why fear neglect?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「我聞載籍：五帝之臣，臣不若君，故君親攬其事；

translations.literal: ' Biao said: 'I have heard in the records: ministers of the Five Emperors were not equal to their lords, so the lords personally handled affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Biao said: 'Records say: under the Five Emperors ministers were lesser than their lords, so lords handled affairs themselves;

sentences.zh: 三王君臣智等，故共理機務；

translations.literal: under the Three Kings ruler and minister were equal in wisdom, so they jointly managed affairs;
translations.idiomatic: under the Three Kings ruler and minister were equal in wisdom and managed affairs together;

sentences.zh: 五霸臣過於君，故事決於下。

translations.literal: under the Five Hegemons ministers surpassed their lords, so decisions lay below.
translations.idiomatic: under the Five Hegemons ministers surpassed their lords, so decisions lay below.

sentences.zh: 我朝官司皆五帝之臣，主上親攬，蓋遠軌軒唐。

translations.literal: Our court's officials are ministers of the Five Emperors; the sovereign personally handles affairs—surely this far surpasses Xuanyuan and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Our officials are like ministers of the Five Emperors; the sovereign handles affairs himself—far surpassing Xuanyuan and Tang.

sentences.zh: 」彪將還，賾親謂曰：「卿前使還日，賦阮詩云『但願長閑暇，後歲復來遊』，果如今日。

translations.literal: When Biao was about to return, Ze personally said to him: 'On your previous mission's return you composed Ruan Ji’s poem, "I only wish long leisure, next year to come again and roam"—truly as today.
translations.idiomatic: As Biao prepared to leave, Xiao Ze said: 'On your last return you quoted Ruan Ji: "I only wish long leisure, to come again next year"—and so it has proved.

sentences.zh: [8]卿此還也，復有來理否？

translations.literal: [8] On this return too, is there reason to come again?
translations.idiomatic: [8] On this return, will there be cause to come again?

sentences.zh: 」彪答言：「使臣請重賦阮詩曰『宴衍清都中，一去永矣哉』。

translations.literal: ' Biao answered: 'Your envoy begs to rework Ruan Ji's poem: "Feasting in the clear capital, once gone—forever gone."'
translations.idiomatic: Biao answered: 'Let me rework Ruan Ji: "Feasting in the clear capital—once gone, gone forever."'

sentences.zh: 」賾惘然曰：「清都可爾，一去何事？

translations.literal: ' Ze said in dismay: 'The clear capital may be so—but once gone, what affair?
translations.idiomatic: Ze said sadly: 'The clear capital may be—but once gone, what then?

sentences.zh: 觀卿此言，似成長闊，朕當以殊禮相送。

translations.literal: Judging by your words, you seem to grow distant; I shall send you off with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Your words sound like growing distance; I shall send you off with special honor.

sentences.zh: 」賾遂親至琅邪城，登山臨水，命羣臣賦詩以送別，其見重如此。
