translations.literal: ' Ze thereupon personally went to Langye city, ascended the mountain and looked on the water, ordered his ministers to compose poems for the farewell—he was honored thus.
translations.idiomatic: Ze went in person to Langye, climbed the mountain and looked on the waters, and had his ministers compose farewell poems—such was Biao's esteem.

sentences.zh: 彪前後六度銜命，南人奇其謇諤。

translations.literal: Biao before and after six times bore credentials; southerners marveled at his blunt remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Biao six times carried imperial credentials; southerners marveled at his blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南征，假彪冠軍將軍、東道副將，尋假征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south, Biao was provisionally made General Who Establishes the Army and Eastern Route deputy commander; soon he was provisionally made General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south, Biao was made provisional General Who Establishes the Army and eastern deputy, then General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京，遷御史中尉，領著作郎。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned to the capital, he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Director of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: On return to the capital he became Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Director of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 彪既為高祖所寵，性又剛直，遂多所劾糾，遠近畏之，豪右屏氣。

translations.literal: Biao, being favored by Gaozu and by nature upright and stern, thereupon impeached many and far and near feared him; powerful families held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Favored by Gaozu and stern by nature, Biao impeached many; the powerful feared him and held their breath.

sentences.zh: 高祖常呼彪為李生，於是從容謂羣臣曰：「吾之有李生，猶漢之有汲黯。

translations.literal: Gaozu often called Biao 'Master Li'; he then said easily to his ministers: 'My having Master Li is like Han's having Ji An.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often called him 'Master Li' and told his ministers: 'Having Li Biao is like Han having Ji An.'

sentences.zh: 」汾州胡叛，詔彪持節綏慰，事寧還京，除散騎常侍，仍領御史中尉，解著作事。

translations.literal: When the Hu rebelled in Fenzhou, an edict ordered Biao to hold credentials and soothe them; when affairs were settled he returned to the capital, was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, still Censor-in-Chief, and relieved of compilation duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu rebels rose in Fenzhou, Biao was sent with credentials to soothe them; on his return he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, still Censor-in-Chief, and relieved of compilation.

sentences.zh: 高祖宴羣臣於流化池，謂僕射李沖曰：「崔光之博，李彪之直，是我國家得賢之基。」

translations.literal: Gaozu feasted ministers at the Flowing Transformation Pool and said to the Steward Cui Guang and Li Chong: 'Cui Guang's breadth and Li Biao's uprightness are the foundation of our state's obtaining worthies.'
translations.idiomatic: At a feast at the Flowing Transformation Pool, Gaozu told Li Chong: 'Cui Guang's learning and Li Biao's uprightness are how our state finds worthy men.'

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，彪兼度支尚書，與僕射李沖、任城王等參理留臺事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Biao was concurrently Minister of Revenue and with the Steward Li Chong and the Prince of Rencheng joined in managing affairs of the capital left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Biao was Minister of Revenue and with Li Chong and the Prince of Rencheng managed the capital in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 彪素性剛豪，與沖等意議乖異，遂形於聲色，殊無降下之心。

translations.literal: Biao by nature was stern and proud; his views differed from Chong and others, and this showed in voice and countenance—he had no mind to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was proud and stern; he clashed with Chong and others openly and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 自謂身為法官，莫能糾劾己者，遂多專恣。

translations.literal: Considering himself judge and beyond impeachment, he grew willful.
translations.idiomatic: As chief judge he thought none could impeach him and grew willful.

sentences.zh: 沖積其前後罪過，乃於尚書省禁止彪，上表曰：「臣聞範國匡人，光化昇治，輿服典章，理無暫失。

translations.literal: Chong accumulated his offenses before and after and had him barred in the Ministry of Works, submitting a memorial: 'Your servant has heard that regulating the state and correcting men, glorifying governance, carriages, dress, and canonical regulations—reason admits no moment's loss.
translations.idiomatic: Chong gathered his offenses and barred him in the Ministry, memorializing: 'Regulating the state, canonical rites and dress—none may lapse even briefly.

sentences.zh: 故晉文功建九合，猶見抑於請隧；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Wen of Jin, though his achievement joined the nine unifications, was still restrained from requesting the tunnel mound;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin, though he joined the nine unifications, was still denied the royal mound;

sentences.zh: 季氏藉政三世，尚受譏於璵璠。

translations.literal: the Ji clan held power three generations yet still received ridicule over jade tablets.
translations.idiomatic: the Ji clan held power three generations yet was ridiculed over jade regalia.

sentences.zh: 固知名器之重，不可以妄假。

translations.literal: Thus the weight of names and vessels must not be rashly lent.
translations.idiomatic: The weight of titles and regalia must not be rashly lent.

sentences.zh: 先王既憲章於古，陛下又經綸於今，用能車服有叙，禮物無墜。

translations.literal: Former kings took the ancient as law; Your Majesty also orders the present—thus carriages and dress are ordered and ritual objects do not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Former kings took antiquity as law; Your Majesty orders the present—carriages, dress, and ritual remain in order.

sentences.zh: 案臣彪昔於凡品，特以才拔，等望清華，司文東觀，綢繆恩眷，繩直憲臺，左加金璫，右珥蟬冕。

translations.literal: Reviewing Biao: from ordinary rank he was specially raised for talent, equal in hope to the pure and splendid, steward of texts at the Eastern Pavilion, bound by grace, straight on the law platform, gold tassel on the left, cicada ornament on the right,
translations.idiomatic: Biao was raised from ordinary rank for talent, served at the Eastern Pavilion, favored with grace, upright on the law platform, gold tassel and cicada ornament,

sentences.zh: 闕東省。

translations.literal: lacking the Eastern Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: yet lacked the Eastern Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宜感恩厲節，忠以報德。

translations.literal: He should be grateful and strengthen integrity, loyal to repay virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He should have been grateful and loyal in repayment.

sentences.zh: 而竊名忝職，身為違傲，矜勢高亢，公行僭逸。

translations.literal: Yet he usurped name and disgraced office, personally violating arrogance, proud of power and lofty, openly transgressing and indulging.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he usurped name and office, arrogant and proud, openly transgressing.

sentences.zh: 坐輿禁省，[9]冒取官材，輒駕乘黃，無所憚懾。

translations.literal: Riding a carriage into the forbidden precinct, [9] taking official materials without right, driving yellow horses at will, without fear.
translations.idiomatic: He rode into the forbidden precinct [9], took official timber, drove imperial horses without fear.

sentences.zh: 肆志傲然，愚聾視聽，此而可忍，誰不可懷！

translations.literal: Willfully arrogant, deaf and blind to oversight—if this can be borne, what cannot be harbored!
translations.idiomatic: Willfully arrogant, deaf to oversight—if this is borne, what outrage cannot be harbored!

sentences.zh: 臣輒集尚書已下、令史已上，并治書侍御史臣酈道元等於尚書都座，以彪所犯罪狀告彪，訊其虛實，若或不知，須訊部下。

translations.literal: Your servant has assembled those from Ministers of Works down and clerks up, with Reviewing Secretary Li Daoyuan and others at the Ministry seat, reporting Biao's crimes to Biao and examining truth; if he does not know, his subordinates must be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: I assembled officials down to clerks, with Li Daoyuan and others, reported his crimes to him and examined the facts.

sentences.zh: 彪答臣言：『事見在目，實如所劾，皆彪所知，何須復召部下。

translations.literal: Biao answered: 'Matters are before the eyes, truly as impeached—all Biao knows; why summon subordinates again?
translations.idiomatic: Biao answered: 'It is all before my eyes, as impeached—I know it all; why summon subordinates?'

sentences.zh: 』臣今請以見事，免彪所居職，付廷尉治獄。」

translations.literal: ' Your servant now asks, on the basis of visible facts, to remove Biao from office and deliver him to the Minister of Justice for trial.'
translations.idiomatic: I ask, on visible facts, to remove Biao from office and deliver him to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 沖又表曰：

translations.literal: Chong again memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 臣與彪相識以來垂二十載，彪始南使之時，見其色厲辭辯、才優學博，臣之愚識，謂是拔萃之一人。

translations.literal: Your servant has known Biao nearly twenty years; when Biao first went south as envoy, I saw his stern color and eloquent debate, excellent talent and broad learning—my foolish knowledge took him for one who stands out.
translations.idiomatic: I have known Biao nearly twenty years; on his first southern mission I saw his stern eloquence and broad learning and took him for a standout.

sentences.zh: 及彪位宦升達，參與言燕，聞彪評章古今，商略人物，興言於侍筵之次，啟論於眾英之中，賞忠識正，發言懇惻，惟直是語，辭無隱避。

translations.literal: When Biao's rank rose and he joined discourse, I heard him appraise past and present and weigh men, speaking at banquets and opening debate among the talented—praising loyalty, knowing rectitude, speaking earnestly, only straight words, words without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: As he rose I heard him appraise past and present at banquets—praising loyalty, speaking straight without concealment.

sentences.zh: 雖復諸王之尊，近侍之要，至有是非，多面抗折。

translations.literal: Though princes were honored and close attendants important, when there was right and wrong he often opposed them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Even princes and close attendants he often opposed to their faces when they were wrong.

sentences.zh: 酷疾矯詐，毒愆非違，厲色正辭，如鷹鸇之逐鳥雀，懍懍然實似公清之操。

translations.literal: He hated harshly those who feigned and sinned against the law, stern in color and correct in words, like a hawk chasing sparrows—stern indeed like the conduct of public rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He hated fraud and lawbreakers, stern as a hawk on sparrows—seeming the conduct of public rectitude.

sentences.zh: 臣雖下才，輒亦尚其梗概，欽其正直，微識其褊急之性，而不以為瑕。

translations.literal: Though your servant is low in talent, I also admired his spirit and honored his uprightness, slightly knowing his impatient nature yet not taking it as flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am low in talent, I admired his spirit and uprightness, knowing his impatience yet not counting it flaw.

sentences.zh: 及其初登憲臺，始居司直，首復騶唱之儀，肇正直繩之體，當時識者僉以為難。

translations.literal: When he first ascended the law platform and first held the office of rectifier, first restoring the ceremony of outriders and establishing the body of straight rope—those who knew at the time all thought it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took the law platform and restored outrider ceremony and the straight rope—all thought it difficult.

sentences.zh: 而彪秉志信行，不避豪勢，其所彈劾，應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Yet Biao held his will and trusted his conduct, not avoiding powerful families; those he impeached fell as if the string were loosed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Biao held his will, did not avoid the powerful, and those he impeached fell at once.

sentences.zh: 赫赫之威，振於下國；

translations.literal: Majestic awe shook the lower states;
translations.idiomatic: His awe shook the regions;

sentences.zh: 肅肅之稱，著自京師。

translations.literal: stern reputation was established from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: his stern name rose from the capital.

sentences.zh: 天下改目，貪暴斂手。

translations.literal: All under heaven changed their eyes; the greedy and violent drew in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven took notice; the greedy and violent drew back.

sentences.zh: 臣時見其所行，信謂言行相符，忠清內發。

translations.literal: Your servant then saw his conduct and truly believed words and deeds matched, loyalty and purity issuing within.
translations.idiomatic: I then saw his conduct and believed words matched deeds, loyalty issuing within.

sentences.zh: 然時有私於臣，云其威暴者，臣以直繩之官，人所忌疾，風謗之際，易生音謠，心不承信。

translations.literal: Yet at the time someone privately told your servant he was fierce and violent; your servant, as straight-roping officer, is what men hate—in times of slander rumors easily arise; the heart did not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet someone said he was fierce; as straight-roping officer he was hated—slander arises easily; I did not believe.

sentences.zh: 往年以河陽事，曾與彪在領軍府，共太尉、司空及領軍諸卿等，集閱廷尉所問囚徒。

translations.literal: In former years on the Heyang affair, I was with Biao at the Army Supervisor's office, together with the Grand Commandant, Minister of Works, and army supervisors, assembling to review prisoners questioned by the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In former years on the Heyang matter I was with Biao at the Army Supervisor's office reviewing prisoners with the Grand Commandant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時有人訴枉者，二公及臣少欲聽採。

translations.literal: When someone appealed injustice, the two dukes and your servant slightly wished to hear and adopt.
translations.idiomatic: When someone appealed injustice, the two dukes and I wished to hear them.

sentences.zh: 語理未盡，彪便振怒，東坐攘袂揮赫，口稱賊奴，叱吒左右，高聲大呼云：「南臺中取我木手去，撘奴肋折！

translations.literal: Before reasoning was finished, Biao grew angry, sat eastward, flung his sleeves and raged, calling them rebel slaves, shouting at attendants, crying loudly: 'South Platform, fetch my wooden hand—break the slave's ribs!'
translations.idiomatic: Before reasoning ended, Biao grew angry, flung his sleeves, called them rebel slaves, and shouted: 'South Platform, fetch my wooden hand—break their ribs!'

sentences.zh: 」雖有此言，終竟不取。

translations.literal: ' Though he said this, in the end he did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Though he said this, he did not take it in the end.

sentences.zh: 即言：「南臺所問，唯恐枉活，終無枉死，但可依此。

translations.literal: He then said: 'What the South Platform questions fears only the guilty living; there is never the guilty dead—only follow this.'
translations.idiomatic: He said: 'The South Platform fears only letting the guilty live—never the innocent dead—follow this.'

sentences.zh: 」時諸人以所枉至重，有首實者多，又心難彪，遂各默爾。

translations.literal: At the time all thought the injustice grave and many confessed; they also resented Biao inwardly and each fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: All thought the injustice grave and many had confessed; resenting Biao, each fell silent.

sentences.zh: 因緣此事，臣遂心疑有濫，審加情察，知其威虐，猶未體其採訪之由，訊檢之狀。

translations.literal: Because of this affair your servant's heart suspected excess; on careful examination I knew his fierceness, yet still did not grasp the reason for his inquiries and examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this I suspected excess; on examination I knew his fierceness, yet not the reason for his inquiries.

sentences.zh: 商略而言，酷急小罪，肅禁為大。

translations.literal: Weighing it, severity on small crimes and stern prohibition were great.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing it, severity on small crimes was great.

sentences.zh: 會而言之，猶謂益多損少。

translations.literal: Summing up, one still said gain outweighed loss.
translations.idiomatic: Summed up, gain still seemed to outweigh loss.

sentences.zh: 故懷寢所疑，不以申徹，實失為臣知無不聞之義。

translations.literal: Therefore I harbored doubt and did not report it—truly failing the minister's duty of knowing and not hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I harbored doubt and did not report—failing the duty to speak.

sentences.zh: 及去年大駕南行以來，彪兼尚書，日夕共事，始乃知其言與行舛，是己非人，專恣無忌，尊身忽物，安己凌上，[10]以身作之過深劾他人，己方事人，好人佞己。

translations.literal: From last year when the great carriage went south, Biao was concurrently Minister of Works and daily shared work—only then did I know his words and deeds diverged, approving himself and disapproving others, willful without restraint, honoring himself and slighting things, securing himself and insulting superiors, [10] deeply impeaching others for faults he himself committed, serving others while wanting flattery for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Since last year's southern journey, sharing work daily, I learned his words and deeds diverged—willful, slighting superiors [10], impeaching others for his own faults, wanting flattery.

sentences.zh: 聽其言同振古忠恕之賢，校其行是天下佞暴之賊。

translations.literal: Hearing his words, one thinks him a sage of ancient loyalty and forbearance; comparing his conduct, he is the flatterer and tyrant of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing him, one thinks a sage of loyalty; comparing conduct, he is the realm's flatterer and tyrant.

sentences.zh: 臣與任城卑躬曲己，若順弟之奉暴兄。

translations.literal: Your servant and the Prince of Rencheng bowed and bent ourselves, like a compliant younger brother serving a violent elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Rencheng and I bowed like compliant younger brothers to a violent elder.

sentences.zh: 其所欲者，事雖非理，無不屈從。

translations.literal: What he desired, though the affair was not reasonable, none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: What he wanted, though unreasonable, none failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 依事求實，悉有成驗。

translations.literal: Seeking truth according to affairs, all had proof.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking truth by facts, all was proved.

sentences.zh: 如臣列得實，宜殛彪於有北，以除姦矯之亂政；

translations.literal: If your servant's list is true, Biao should be executed in the north to remove corrupt flattery from government;
translations.idiomatic: If my list is true, Biao should be executed in the north to remove corrupt flattery;

sentences.zh: 如臣無證，宜投臣於四裔，以息青蠅之白黑。

translations.literal: if your servant has no proof, your servant should be cast to the four borders to still the blue flies' black and white.
translations.idiomatic: if I have no proof, cast me to the four borders to still slander.

sentences.zh: 高祖在懸瓠，覽表歎愕曰：「何意留京如此也！

translations.literal: Gaozu at Xuanhu, reading the memorial, sighed in alarm: 'Who thought the capital would be thus!'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu at Xuanhu, reading the memorial, sighed: 'Who thought the capital would be thus!'

sentences.zh: 」有司處彪大辟，高祖恕之，除名而已。

translations.literal: ' The relevant offices sentenced Biao to great execution; Gaozu pardoned him—removal of name only.
translations.idiomatic: The offices sentenced him to death; Gaozu pardoned him—name removed only.

sentences.zh: 彪尋歸本鄉。

translations.literal: Biao soon returned to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: Biao soon returned home.

sentences.zh: 高祖自懸瓠北幸鄴，彪拜迎於鄴南。

translations.literal: Gaozu from Xuanhu went north to Ye; Biao bowed to welcome him south of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu went north from Xuanhu to Ye; Biao welcomed him south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕之期卿。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: 'I have long expected you.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: 'I have long expected you.

sentences.zh: 每以貞松為志，歲寒為心，卿應報國，盡身為用，而近見彈文，殊乖所以。

translations.literal: Always taking the steadfast pine as resolve and cold years as heart—you should repay the state and exhaust yourself in service; yet recently I see impeachment documents—quite contrary to my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the steadfast pine as resolve and cold years as heart—you should serve the state; yet recent impeachments are contrary to my intent.

sentences.zh: 卿罹此譴，為朕與卿，為宰事與卿，為卿自取？

translations.literal: You suffer this punishment—for me and you, for the steward and you, or for what you brought on yourself?
translations.idiomatic: You suffer this—for me and you, for the steward and you, or for yourself?

sentences.zh: 」彪對曰：「臣愆由己至，罪自身招，實非陛下橫與臣罪，又非宰事無辜濫臣。

translations.literal: ' Biao answered: 'Your servant's fault came from himself, guilt invited by himself—truly not Your Majesty wrongly giving guilt, nor the steward wrongly implicating your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Biao answered: 'My fault came from myself—not Your Majesty's wrongful guilt, nor the steward's wrongful charge.

sentences.zh: 臣罪既如此，宜伏東皐之下，不應遠點屬車之塵，但伏承聖躬不豫，臣肝膽塗地，是以敢至，非謝罪而來。

translations.literal: Your servant's guilt being thus, I should lie prostrate below the eastern ridge and not approach the dust of the entourage; but I heard the sage person is unwell—your servant's liver and gall are smeared on the ground; therefore I dare come—not to beg pardon.
translations.idiomatic: I should lie prostrate in exile, not approach the entourage; but hearing Your Majesty is unwell, my heart is torn—that is why I came, not to beg pardon.

sentences.zh: 」高祖納宋弁言，將復採用，會留臺表言彪與御史賈尚往窮庶人恂事，理有誣抑，奏請收彪。

translations.literal: ' Gaozu accepted Song Bian's words and was about to employ him again; the capital memorial reported Biao and Censor Jia Shang had gone to investigate the commoner Xun affair, the case having false suppression, and requested Biao be arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted Song Bian's counsel and would employ him again; the capital reported Biao and Censor Jia Shang investigated the commoner Xun with false suppression and asked to arrest Biao.

sentences.zh: 彪自言事枉，高祖明彪無此，遣左右慰勉之，聽以牛車散載，送之洛陽。

translations.literal: Biao said the affair was unjust; Gaozu knew Biao had not done this, sent attendants to comfort him, and permitted him to return to Luoyang scattered in ox carts.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said it was unjust; Gaozu knew he had not done this, comforted him, and let him return to Luoyang in ox carts.

sentences.zh: 會赦得免。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，世宗踐祚，彪自託於王肅，又與邢巒詩書往來，迭相稱重，因論求復舊職，修史官之事，肅等許為左右，彪乃表曰：

translations.literal: When Gaozu died and Emperor Shizong ascended, Biao entrusted himself to Wang Su and also exchanged poems and letters with Xing Luan, each praising the other; he discussed seeking restoration to old office and repairing the historiographer's affairs—Su and others promised support—and Biao thereupon memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died and Emperor Shizong ascended, Biao relied on Wang Su and exchanged poems with Xing Luan; they praised each other and he sought restoration and repair of the historiographer's office—Su promised support—and Biao memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞龍圖出而皇道明，龜書見而帝德昶，斯實冥中之書契也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard: when the dragon chart appears, imperial Way is clear; when the tortoise book appears, imperial virtue is bright—this is truly the covenant of the hidden realm.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard: when the dragon chart appears the imperial Way is clear; when the tortoise book appears imperial virtue shines—this is the covenant of the hidden realm.

sentences.zh: 自瑞官文而卑高陳，[11]民師建而賤貴序，此乃人間之繩式也。

translations.literal: From the auspicious officials' patterns, low and high are displayed; [11] when people's teachers are established, base and noble are ordered—this is the measuring cord of the human realm.
translations.idiomatic: From auspicious patterns low and high are set; [11] when teachers of the people are established, base and noble are ordered—the measuring cord of the human realm.

sentences.zh: 是以唐典篆欽明之冊，虞書銘慎徽之篇，傳著夏氏之箴，詩錄商家之頌，斯皆國史明乎得失之迹也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Tang canon inscribed the book of reverent clarity; the Yu documents engraved the chapter of cautious emblems; the Documents recorded the Xia clan's admonitions; the Odes recorded the Shang house's hymns—all national histories clarifying the traces of gain and loss.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang canon inscribed reverent clarity; the Yu documents engraved cautious emblems; the Documents recorded Xia admonitions; the Odes recorded Shang hymns—all histories clarifying gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 逮于周姬，鑒乎二代，文王開之以兩經，公旦申之以六聯，郁乎其文，典章大略也。

translations.literal: Reaching the Zhou house, taking the two dynasties as mirror, King Wen opened it with the two classics, the Duke of Zhou extended it with the six links—rich in text, the great outline of institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou, mirroring the two prior dynasties, King Wen opened with the two classics, the Duke of Zhou extended with the six links—rich text, the great outline of institutions.

sentences.zh: 故觀雅、頌，識文武之丕烈；

translations.literal: Therefore observing the Ya and Song, one knows the great glory of Wen and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Observing the Ya and Song, one knows the great glory of Wen and Wu;

sentences.zh: 察歌音，辨周公之至孝。

translations.literal: examining songs and tones, one distinguishes the Duke of Zhou's utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: examining songs and tones, one sees the Duke of Zhou's utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 是以季札聽風而知始基，聽頌而識盛德。

translations.literal: Therefore Ji Zha, hearing the winds, knew the beginning foundation; hearing the hymns, knew flourishing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zha, hearing the winds, knew the founding; hearing the hymns, knew flourishing virtue.

sentences.zh: 至若尼父之別魯籍，丘明之辨孔志，可謂婉而成章，盡而不汚者矣。

translations.literal: As for the Master distinguishing the Lu records, Qiu Ming clarifying Confucius's intent—one may call it graceful in completion, exhaustive yet not defiled.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius distinguishing the Lu records, Zuo Qiuming clarifying Confucius's intent—graceful, exhaustive, yet not defiled.

sentences.zh: 自餘乘、志之比，其亦有趣焉。

translations.literal: Among the rest, the Cheng and Zhi and the like also have their interest.
translations.idiomatic: Among the rest, Cheng and Zhi and the like also have their interest.

sentences.zh: 暨史、班之錄，乃文窮於秦漢，事盡於哀平，懲勸兩書，華實兼載，文質彬彬，富哉言也。

translations.literal: Reaching the records of Shi and Ban, text ends at Qin and Han, affairs end at Ai and Ping—the two books of warning and encouragement, flower and fruit both loaded, wen and quality balanced—rich indeed the words.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ji and Han Shu end at Qin-Han, affairs at Ai and Ping—two books of warning and encouragement, substance and style balanced—rich indeed.

sentences.zh: 令大漢之風，美類三代，炎□□崇，道冠來事。

translations.literal: Now the Great Han's wind, beautiful like the Three Dynasties, flame [damaged text] exalted, the Way crowns coming affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Han's wind, beautiful as the Three Dynasties, flame and glory exalted, the Way crowning ages to come.

sentences.zh: 降及華、馬、陳、干，[12]咸有放焉，四。

translations.literal: Descending to Hua, Ma, Chen, and Gan, [12] all had followers; four.
translations.idiomatic: Descending to Hua, Ma, Chen, and Gan [12], all had followers.

sentences.zh: 敷贊弗遠，[13]不可力致，豈虛也哉？

translations.literal: Spreading praise not far, [13] cannot be forced to arrive—is it empty?
translations.idiomatic: Spreading praise far and wide [13] cannot be forced—is it empty?

sentences.zh: 其餘率見而書，覩事而作者多矣，尋其本末，可往來焉。

translations.literal: The rest mostly seeing and writing, beholding affairs and composing—many indeed; tracing root and branch, one may go back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: Others mostly wrote what they saw and composed on what they witnessed—many indeed; tracing root and branch, one may go back and forth.

sentences.zh: 唯我皇魏之奄有中華也，歲越百齡，年幾十紀。

translations.literal: Only our august Wei, covering the central states—years surpass a century, ages nearly ten cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Only our august Wei, covering the central states—years beyond a century, ages nearly ten cycles.

sentences.zh: 太祖以弗違開基，武皇以奉時拓業，虎嘯域中，龍飛宇外，小往大來，品物咸亨，自茲以降。

translations.literal: Taizu with non-transgression opened the foundation; Wuhuang with following the times expanded the enterprise—tiger roaring within the realm, dragon flying beyond the four seas; small going, great coming, all things prosperous—from this down.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu opened the foundation without transgression; Wuhuang expanded the enterprise in season—tiger roaring within the realm, dragon flying beyond the seas; from small to great all things prospered—from then until now.

sentences.zh: 世濟其光。

translations.literal: Generations continue its radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation continues its radiance.

sentences.zh: 史官敍錄，未充其盛。

translations.literal: Historians' records have not filled its fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Historians' records have not matched its fullness.

sentences.zh: 加以東觀中圮，冊勳有闕，美隨日落，善因月稀。

translations.literal: Added to this, the Eastern Pavilion mid-collapsed, meritorious registers have gaps; beauty follows the sun in setting, goodness grows sparse with the moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Pavilion collapsed midway; registers of merit have gaps; beauty fades like the setting sun, goodness grows sparse.

sentences.zh: 故諺曰：「一日不書，百事荒蕪。

translations.literal: Therefore the proverb says: 'One day without writing—a hundred affairs lie waste.
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says: 'One day without writing—a hundred affairs lie waste.'

sentences.zh: 」至于太和之十一年，先帝、先后遠惟景業，綿綿休烈，若不恢史闡錄，懼上業茂功始有缺矣。

translations.literal: ' Reaching the eleventh year of Taihe, the late emperor and empress dowager far contemplated the splendid enterprise, continuous glorious achievements—if history is not broadly restored and recorded, I fear the upper enterprise's abundant merit will at first have gaps.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh year of Taihe, the late emperor and empress far contemplated the splendid enterprise—if history is not broadly restored, the upper enterprise's merit will have gaps.

sentences.zh: 於是召名儒博達之士，充麟閣之選。

translations.literal: Thereupon famous Confucians and broadly accomplished scholars were summoned to fill the Qilin Pavilion's selection.
translations.idiomatic: Famous Confucians and accomplished scholars were summoned to fill the Qilin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 于時忘臣眾短，采臣片志，令臣出納，授臣丞職，猥屬斯事，無所與讓。

translations.literal: At that time forgetting your servant's many shortcomings, gathering your servant's slight will, ordering your servant in and out, granting your servant assistant rank—humbly attached to this affair, with nothing to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Then forgetting my many faults, gathering my slight will, ordering me in and out, granting assistant rank—I was humbly attached to this affair.

sentences.zh: 高祖時詔臣曰：「平爾雅志，正爾筆端，書而不法，後世何觀。

translations.literal: Gaozu then ordered your servant: 'Level your elegant will, correct your brush tip; write without law—what will later generations observe?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered me: 'Level your elegant will, correct your brush; write without law—what will later generations see?'

sentences.zh: 」臣奉以周旋，不敢失墜，與著作等鳩集遺文，并取前記，撰為國書。

translations.literal: ' Your servant received this and turned in it, not daring to fail, and with the compilers gathered surviving texts and also took former records to compile the national book.
translations.idiomatic: I received this and did not dare fail; with the compilers I gathered surviving texts and former records to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 假有新進時賢制作於此者，恐閨門既異，出入生疑，弦柱既易，善者或謬。

translations.literal: If there are newly advanced worthies of the time composing here, I fear the inner gate will differ, going in and out will breed doubt; if string and pillar are already changed, the good may err.
translations.idiomatic: If newly advanced scholars compose here, the inner gate will differ and doubt will arise; if the framework changes, even the good may err.

sentences.zh: [14]自十五年以來，臣使國遷，頻有南轅之事，故載筆遂寢，簡牘弗張，其於書功錄美，不其闕歟？

translations.literal: [14] From the fifteenth year onward, your servant's missions shifted the state, frequently having southern carriage affairs—therefore the recording brush was laid to rest, bamboo slips not spread; as for writing merit and recording beauty—is it not a gap?
translations.idiomatic: [14] From the fifteenth year my missions shifted the state, with frequent southern journeys—the brush rested, slips were not spread; writing merit and recording beauty—was it not a gap?

sentences.zh: 伏惟孝文皇帝承天地之寶，崇祖宗之業，景功未就，奄焉崩殞，凡百黎萌，若無天地。

translations.literal: I bow before Emperor Xiaowen, who received Heaven and Earth's treasure, honored the ancestors' enterprise—splendid achievement not yet completed, suddenly collapsed and died; the hundred surnames' sprouts were as without Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen received Heaven and Earth's treasure and honored the ancestors' enterprise—splendid achievement unfinished, he suddenly died; the people were as if without Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 賴遇陛下體明叡之真，應保合之量，恢大明以燭物，履靜恭以安邦，天清其氣，地樂其靜，不愆不忘，率由舊章，可謂重明疊聖，元首康哉。

translations.literal: Fortunately encountering Your Majesty embodying bright sagacity, responding to the measure of preserving harmony, extending great clarity to illumine things, treading quiet reverence to settle the state—Heaven clears its qi, Earth delights in its stillness, without fault, without forgetting, following the old statutes—one may call it repeated brightness piled sage, the head restored and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Your Majesty embodies bright sagacity, extends great clarity, treads quiet reverence to settle the state—Heaven clears, Earth rests, without fault, following old statutes—repeated brightness, the head at ease.

sentences.zh: 惟先皇之開創造物，經綸浩曠，加以魏典流製，藻繢垂篇，窮理於有象，盡性於眾變，可謂日月出矣，無幽不燭也。

translations.literal: Only the late emperor's opening creation and making things, ordering the vast expanse, added to Wei's flowing institutions and patterned chapters hanging in volumes, exhausting principle in images, exhausting nature in myriad changes—one may call it the sun and moon have risen, nothing hidden unillumined.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's creation ordered the vast expanse; Wei's flowing institutions and patterned chapters exhaust principle in images and nature in change—the sun and moon have risen, nothing hidden unlit.

sentences.zh: 記曰：善流者欲以繼其行，善歌者欲人繼其聲。

translations.literal: The Record says: Those good at flowing wish to continue their conduct; those good at singing wish men to continue their sound.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: Those good at flowing wish to continue conduct; those good at singing wish others to continue their sound.

sentences.zh: [15]故傳曰：文王基之，周公成之。

translations.literal: [15] Therefore the Documents say: King Wen laid the foundation, the Duke of Zhou completed it.
translations.idiomatic: [15] The Documents say: King Wen laid the foundation, the Duke of Zhou completed it.

sentences.zh: 又曰：無周公之才，不得行周公之事。

translations.literal: It also says: Without the Duke of Zhou's talent, one cannot perform the Duke of Zhou's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: Without the Duke of Zhou's talent one cannot perform the Duke of Zhou's affairs.

sentences.zh: 今之親王，可謂當之矣。

translations.literal: Today's imperial princes may be called equal to it.
translations.idiomatic: Today's imperial princes may be called equal to it.

sentences.zh: 然先皇之茂猷聖達，今王之懿美洞鑒，準之前代，其聽靡悔也。

translations.literal: Yet the late emperor's abundant plans were sage and penetrating; the present king's excellent beauty is clear-sighted—measured against former ages, his listening is without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's plans were sage and penetrating; the present king's excellence is clear-sighted—measured against former ages, his listening is without regret.

sentences.zh: 時哉時哉，可不光昭哉！

translations.literal: The time! The time! How can it not shine forth!
translations.idiomatic: The time! The time! How can it not shine forth!

sentences.zh: 合德二儀者，先皇之陶鈞也；

translations.literal: Harmonizing virtue with the two Powers— the late emperor's pottery wheel;
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing virtue with Heaven and Earth—the late emperor's pottery wheel;

sentences.zh: 齊明日月者，先皇之洞照也；

translations.literal: equal in clarity to sun and moon—the late emperor's penetrating illumination;
translations.idiomatic: equal in clarity to sun and moon—the late emperor's illumination;

sentences.zh: 慮周四時者，先皇之茂功也；

translations.literal: considering and encompassing the four seasons—the late emperor's abundant achievement;
translations.idiomatic: considering the four seasons—the late emperor's abundant achievement;

sentences.zh: 合契鬼神者，先皇之玄燭也；

translations.literal: matching contract with ghosts and spirits—the late emperor's dark torch;
translations.idiomatic: matching contract with ghosts and spirits—the late emperor's dark torch;

sentences.zh: 遷都改邑者，先皇之達也；

translations.literal: moving the capital and changing the settlement—the late emperor's penetration;
translations.idiomatic: moving the capital—the late emperor's penetration;

sentences.zh: 變是協和者，先皇之鑒也；

translations.literal: changing this and harmonizing—the late emperor's mirror;
translations.idiomatic: changing this and harmonizing—the late emperor's mirror;

sentences.zh: 思同書軌者，先皇之遠也；

translations.literal: thinking to equal books and cart-tracks—the late emperor's reach;
translations.idiomatic: thinking to equal books and cart-tracks—the late emperor's reach;

sentences.zh: 守在四夷者，先皇之略也；

translations.literal: guarding at the four barbarians—the late emperor's strategy;
translations.idiomatic: guarding at the four barbarians—the late emperor's strategy;

sentences.zh: 海外有截者，先皇之威也；

translations.literal: overseas having boundaries cut—the late emperor's awe;
translations.idiomatic: overseas having boundaries cut—the late emperor's awe;

sentences.zh: 禮田岐陽者，先皇之義也；

translations.literal: ritual fields at Qiyang—the late emperor's righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: ritual fields at Qiyang—the late emperor's righteousness;

sentences.zh: 張樂岱郊者，先皇之仁也；

translations.literal: spreading music at Dai's suburb—the late emperor's benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: spreading music at Dai's suburb—the late emperor's benevolence;

sentences.zh: 鑾幸幽漠者，先皇之智也；

translations.literal: imperial carriage visiting the dark desert—the late emperor's wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: imperial carriage visiting the dark desert—the late emperor's wisdom;

sentences.zh: 燮伐南荊者，先皇之禮也；

translations.literal: harmonizing campaign against southern Jing—the late emperor's ritual;
translations.idiomatic: harmonizing campaign against southern Jing—the late emperor's ritual;

sentences.zh: 升中告成者，先皇之肅也；

translations.literal: ascending the central peak and reporting completion—the late emperor's solemnity;
translations.idiomatic: ascending the central peak and reporting completion—the late emperor's solemnity;

sentences.zh: 親虔宗社者，先皇之敬也；

translations.literal: personally reverent to the ancestral temple—the late emperor's respect;
translations.idiomatic: personally reverent to the ancestral temple—the late emperor's respect;

sentences.zh: 袞實無闕者，先皇之充也；

translations.literal: imperial robes solid without lack—the late emperor's fullness;
translations.idiomatic: imperial robes solid without lack—the late emperor's fullness;

sentences.zh: 開物成務者，先皇之貞也；

translations.literal: opening things and completing affairs—the late emperor's constancy;
translations.idiomatic: opening things and completing affairs—the late emperor's constancy;

sentences.zh: 觀乎人文者，先皇之蘊也；

translations.literal: observing human patterns—the late emperor's store;
translations.idiomatic: observing human patterns—the late emperor's store;

sentences.zh: 革弊創新者，先皇之志也；

translations.literal: reforming abuses and creating the new—the late emperor's will;
translations.idiomatic: reforming abuses and creating anew—the late emperor's will;

sentences.zh: 孝慈道洽者，先皇之衷也。

translations.literal: filial compassion's Way harmonized—the late emperor's innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: filial compassion harmonized—the late emperor's innermost heart.

sentences.zh: 先皇有大功二十，加以謙尊而光，為而弗有，可謂四三皇而六五帝矣，誠宜功書於竹素，聲播於金石。

translations.literal: The late emperor had twenty great achievements; adding humility and honor to brightness, acting yet not possessing—one may call it four Three Emperors and six Five Emperors; truly merit should be written on bamboo and silk, sound spread on metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor had twenty great achievements; humble yet bright, acting yet not possessing—four Three Emperors and six Five Emperors; merit should be written on bamboo and silk, sound on metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂史官之達者，大則與日月齊明，小則與四時並茂。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that accomplished historiographers, great then equal sun and moon, small then flourish with the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplished historiographers, great as sun and moon, small as the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 其大者孔子、左丘是也，小者史遷、班固是也。

translations.literal: The great: Confucius and Zuo Qiu; the small: Shi Qian and Ban Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The great: Confucius and Zuo Qiuming; the small: Sima Qian and Ban Gu.

sentences.zh: 故能聲流於無窮，義昭於來裔。

translations.literal: Therefore sound flows without end, meaning shines on coming generations.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore sound flows without end, meaning shines on coming generations.

sentences.zh: 是以金石可滅而流風不泯者，其唯載籍乎？

translations.literal: Thus metal and stone may perish yet flowing wind does not die—is it not only the written records?
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone may perish yet flowing wind does not die—is it not only written records?

sentences.zh: 諺曰「相門有相，將門有將」，斯不唯其性，蓋言習之所得也。

translations.literal: The proverb says 'the minister's gate has ministers, the general's gate has generals'—this is not only nature; it mostly speaks of what habit obtains.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says 'the minister's gate has ministers, the general's gate has generals'—not only nature but what habit obtains.

sentences.zh: 竊謂天文之官，太史之職，如有其人，宜其世矣。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers the office of astronomy, the Grand Historian's post—if there is such a person, it should be hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian's post—if there is such a person, it should be hereditary.

sentences.zh: 故尚書稱羲和世掌天地之官，張衡賦曰「學乎舊史氏」，斯蓋世傳之義也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Documents call Xi and He generations in charge of Heaven and Earth's offices; Zhang Heng's rhapsody says 'study with the old Historian's clan'—this is the meaning of transmission through generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents call Xi and He generations in charge of Heaven and Earth; Zhang Heng wrote 'study with the old Historian's clan'—transmission through generations.

sentences.zh: 若夫良冶之子善知為裘，良弓之子善知為箕，物豈有定，習貫則知耳。

translations.literal: If the good smith's son knows how to make fur, the good bowyer's son knows how to make frames—things have no fixity; through habit one knows.
translations.idiomatic: The good smith's son knows fur, the good bowyer's son knows frames—through habit one knows.

sentences.zh: 所以言及此者，史職不修，事多淪曠，天人之際，不可須臾闕載也。

translations.literal: The reason for speaking of this: historiography is not repaired, affairs mostly fall into oblivion—the boundary of Heaven and man cannot lack recording even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Historiography unrepaired, affairs fall into oblivion—the boundary of Heaven and man cannot lack recording even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 是以談遷世事而功立，彪固世事而名成，此乃前鑒之軌轍，[16]後鏡之蓍龜也。

translations.literal: Therefore Tan Qian followed worldly affairs and achievement was established; Biao Gu followed worldly affairs and name was completed—this is the former mirror's track, [16] the later mirror's divination tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Qian followed worldly affairs and achieved; Ban Gu followed worldly affairs and made a name—former mirror's track [16], later mirror's tortoise.

sentences.zh: 然前代史官之不終業者有之，皆陵遲之世不能容善。

translations.literal: Yet there were former-age historiographers who did not finish their work—all were ages of decline that could not contain the good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet former historiographers who did not finish—all were declining ages that could not contain the good.

sentences.zh: 是以平子去史而成賦，伯喈違閣而就志。

translations.literal: Therefore Pingzi left historiography and completed a rhapsody; Boyong left the pavilion and undertook a monograph.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng left historiography and completed a rhapsody; Cai Yong left the pavilion and undertook a monograph.

sentences.zh: 近僭晉之世有佐郎王隱，為著作虞預所毀，亡官在家，晝則樵薪供爨，夜則觀文屬綴，集成晉書，存一代之事，司馬紹敕尚書唯給筆札而已。

translations.literal: In recent usurping Jin's age there was Assistant Gentleman Wang Yin, destroyed by Compiler Yu Yu—office lost, at home; by day gathering firewood for cooking, by night reading texts and linking chapters, compiling Jin History, preserving one generation's affairs—Sima Shao ordered the Ministry of Works to give only brush and paper.
translations.idiomatic: In usurping Jin, Assistant Gentleman Wang Yin was destroyed by Yu Yu—office lost, at home; by day gathering firewood, by night writing, compiling Jin History—Sima Shao ordered only brush and paper.

sentences.zh: 國之大籍，成於私家，末世之弊，乃至如此，史官之不遇，時也。

translations.literal: The state's great register completed in a private house—an end-age abuse reaching thus; the historiographer's ill fortune—timing.
translations.idiomatic: The state's great register completed in a private house—end-age abuse; the historiographer's ill fortune—timing.

sentences.zh: 今大魏之史，職則身貴，祿則親榮，優哉游哉，式穀爾休矣，而典謨弗恢者，其有以也。

translations.literal: Now Great Wei's historiography: office then body honored, salary then kin glorified—easy and at ease, thus grain and rest—yet canon and plan not broadly restored—there is reason.
translations.idiomatic: Great Wei's historiography: office honored, salary glorious—yet canon not broadly restored—there is reason.

sentences.zh: 而故著作漁陽傅毗、北平陽尼、河門邢產、廣平宋弁、昌黎韓顯宗等，並以文才見舉，注述是同，皆登年不永，弗終茂績。

translations.literal: Former compilers Fu Pi of Yuyang, Yang Ni of Beiping, Xing Chan of Hejian, Song Bian of Guangping, Han Xianzong of Changli—all raised for literary talent, annotation and compilation the same—all ascended years not long, did not finish flourishing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Former compilers Fu Pi, Yang Ni, Xing Chan, Song Bian, Han Xianzong—all raised for literary talent—none lived long, none finished flourishing achievement.

sentences.zh: 前著作程靈虬同時應舉，共掌此務，今從他職，官非所司。

translations.literal: Former compiler Cheng Lingqiu at the same time answered the summons, together in charge of this duty; now follows other office, post not what he manages.
translations.idiomatic: Former compiler Cheng Lingqiu answered the summons together; now follows other office, post not what he manages.

sentences.zh: 唯崔光一人，雖不移任，然侍官兩兼，故載述致闕。

translations.literal: Only Cui Guang alone, though not shifting post, yet attendant office doubly combined—therefore compilation and narration have gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cui Guang, though not shifting post, yet doubly combined in attendant office—compilation has gaps.

sentences.zh: 臣聞載籍之興，由於大業，雅頌垂薦，起於德美，雖時有文質，史有備略，然歷世相仍，不改此度也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that written records arise from great enterprise; Ya and Song hang recommendation, rising from virtue's beauty—though times have wen and quality, histories have fullness and brevity, yet passing generations continue without changing this measure.
translations.idiomatic: Written records arise from great enterprise; hymns rise from virtue's beauty—though times differ, generations continue without changing this measure.

sentences.zh: 昔史談誡其子遷曰：「當世有美而不書，汝之罪也。

translations.literal: In former times Shi Tan admonished his son Qian: 'When the age has beauty and you do not write—it is your crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tan admonished his son Qian: 'When the age has beauty and you do not write—it is your crime.'

sentences.zh: 」是以久而見美。

translations.literal: ' Therefore long afterward beauty is seen.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore long afterward beauty is seen.

sentences.zh: 孔明在蜀，不以史官留意，是以久而受譏。

translations.literal: Kongming in Shu did not take historiography to heart—therefore long afterward he received ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang in Shu did not heed historiography—therefore long afterward he was ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 取之深衷，史談之志賢亮遠矣。

translations.literal: Taking the deep intent, Shi Tan's will was worthy, bright, and far.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the deep intent, Shi Tan's will was worthy, bright, and far.

sentences.zh: 書稱「無曠庶官」，詩有「職思其憂」，臣雖今非所司，然昔忝斯任，故不以草茅自疏，敢言及於此。

translations.literal: The Documents call 'no idle offices among the multitude'; the Odes have 'in office, think of worry'—your servant though now not in charge, yet formerly disgraced this post; therefore not taking grass-thatched self as distant, I dare speak to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents call 'no idle offices'; the Odes have 'in office, think of worry'—though not now in charge, I formerly held this post and dare speak.

sentences.zh: 語曰「患為之者不必知，知之者不得為」，臣誠不知，強欲為之耳。

translations.literal: The saying goes 'those who worry to do need not know; those who know cannot do'—your servant truly does not know, yet strongly wishes to do it.
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes 'those who worry to do need not know; those who know cannot do'—I truly do not know, yet strongly wish to do it.

sentences.zh: 竊尋先朝賜臣名彪者，遠則擬漢史之叔皮，近則準晉史之紹統，推名求義，欲罷不能，荷恩佩澤，死而後已。

translations.literal: Your servant privately traces the former court's bestowing the name Biao on me: far then matching Han history's Shupi, near then standarding Jin history's Shaotong—pushing name to seek meaning, wishing to stop yet cannot, bearing grace wearing favor, until death.
translations.idiomatic: The court bestowed the name Biao: far matching Han's Shupi, near matching Jin's Shaotong—bearing grace until death.

sentences.zh: 今求都下乞一靜處，綜理國籍，以終前志，官給事力，以充所須。

translations.literal: Now I request in the capital a quiet place, comprehensively ordering the national registers to finish former intent, offices supplying labor power to fill what is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Now I request a quiet place in the capital to order the national registers and finish my intent, with official support.

sentences.zh: 雖不能光啟大錄，庶不為飽食終日耳。

translations.literal: Though I cannot broadly open the great record, I hope not to be sated with food all day.
translations.idiomatic: Though I cannot broadly open the great record, I hope not to eat my fill all day doing nothing.

sentences.zh: 近則期月可就，遠也三年有成，正本蘊之麟閣，副貳藏之名山。

translations.literal: Near then a month may suffice; far then three years will have achievement—correct copy stored in Qilin Pavilion, duplicate stored in famous mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Near: a month may suffice; far: three years—correct copy in Qilin Pavilion, duplicate in the famous mountain.

sentences.zh: 時司空北海王詳、尚書令王肅以其無祿，頗相賑餉，遂在祕書省同王隱故事，白衣修史。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Prince Xiang of Beihai and Minister of Works Wang Su, because he had no salary, quite aided him; he was then in the Secretariat on Wang Yin's precedent, white-robed compiling history.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Beihai and Wang Su, because he had no salary, aided him; he compiled history in white robes at the Secretariat on Wang Yin's precedent.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，崔光表曰：「伏見前御史中尉臣李彪，夙懷美意，創刊魏典，臣昔為彪所致，與之同業積年，其志力貞強，考述無倦，督勸羣僚，注綴略舉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally governed, Cui Guang memorialized: 'I bow before former Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, from old cherishing fine intent, founding compilation of Wei canon; your servant was once brought by Biao, sharing work many years—his will and strength upright and strong, examining and narrating without weariness, supervising and urging the multitude, annotation and linking slightly raised.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong governed, Cui Guang memorialized: 'Former Censor-in-Chief Li Biao from old founded the Wei canon; I shared work with him many years—his will upright, examining without weariness.

sentences.zh: 雖頃來契闊，多所廢離，近蒙收起，還綜厥事。

translations.literal: Though recently estranged, much abandoned and separated, recently favored to be gathered and return to comprehensive affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though recently estranged and much abandoned, recently gathered to return to comprehensive affairs.

sentences.zh: 老而彌厲，史才日新，若克復舊職，專功不殆，必能昭明春秋，闡成皇籍。

translations.literal: Old yet more stern, historiographic talent daily new—if he can recover old office and specialize without slackening, he will surely clarify Spring and Autumn and complete the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: Old yet more stern, talent daily new—if he recovers old office and specializes, he will clarify Spring and Autumn and complete the imperial register.

sentences.zh: 既先帝厚委，宿歷高班，纖負微愆，應從滌洗。

translations.literal: Since the late emperor thickly entrusted, long ranking high grade, slight bearing of small fault should follow washing away.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late emperor entrusted him and he long ranked high, slight fault should be washed away.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜申以常伯，正綰著作，停其外役，展其內思，研積歲月，紀冊必就。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant considers it fitting to extend him as regular minister, properly holding compilation, stopping his outer service, extending his inner thought—research accumulating months and years, registers will surely be completed.
translations.idiomatic: I consider it fitting to make him regular minister, properly holding compilation, stopping outer service—months and years of research, registers will be completed.

sentences.zh: 鴻聲巨迹，蔚乎有章，盛軌懋詠，鑠焉無泯矣。

translations.literal: Great sound and huge traces, luxuriant and with pattern; flourishing tracks and earnest hymns, shining without perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Great sound and huge traces, luxuriant with pattern; flourishing tracks and earnest hymns, shining without perishing.

sentences.zh: 」世宗不許。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Shizong did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong did not permit.

sentences.zh: 詔彪兼通直散騎常侍，行汾州事，非彪好也，固請不行，有司切遣之。

translations.literal: An edict made Biao concurrently Regular Attendant Directly Communicating, acting Fenzhou affairs—not Biao's preference; he firmly requested not to go; the relevant offices urgently sent him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Biao concurrently Regular Attendant Directly Communicating, acting Fenzhou—not his preference; he firmly refused; the offices urgently sent him.

sentences.zh: 會遘疾累旬，景明二年秋，卒於洛陽，年五十八。

translations.literal: He met illness many tens of days; in autumn of the second year of Jingming he died in Luoyang, age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill for many days; in autumn of Jingming year 2 he died in Luoyang, age fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 始彪為中尉，號為嚴酷，以姦款難得，乃為木手擊其脇腋，氣絕而復屬者時有焉。

translations.literal: At first when Biao was Censor-in-Chief, he was called stern and harsh; because crafty pleas were hard to obtain, he made a wooden hand to strike their ribs and armpits—those whose breath stopped and revived were sometimes seen.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao was Censor-in-Chief he was called stern; because crafty pleas were hard to obtain, he made a wooden hand to strike ribs and armpits—some whose breath stopped revived.

sentences.zh: 又慰喻汾州叛胡，得其兇渠，皆鞭面殺之。

translations.literal: Also soothing the rebel Hu of Fenzhou, obtaining their vicious leaders—all were flogged on the face and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Also soothing the rebel Hu of Fenzhou, obtaining vicious leaders—all were flogged on the face and killed.

sentences.zh: 及彪之病也，體上往往瘡潰，痛毒備極。

translations.literal: When Biao fell ill, on his body sores often ulcerated; pain and poison were extreme.
translations.idiomatic: When Biao fell ill, sores often ulcerated on his body; pain was extreme.

sentences.zh: 詔賜帛一百五十匹，贈鎮遠將軍、汾州刺史，諡曰剛憲。

translations.literal: An edict granted one hundred fifty bolts of silk, posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Fenzhou; posthumous title Gangxian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted one hundred fifty bolts of silk, posthumously General Who Pacifies the Distance and Inspector of Fenzhou; posthumous title Gangxian.

sentences.zh: 彪在祕書歲餘，史業竟未及就，然區分書體，皆彪之功。

translations.literal: Biao was in the Secretariat more than a year; historiographic work in the end was not completed, yet distinguishing book forms was all Biao's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was in the Secretariat over a year; the history was not finished, yet distinguishing book forms was his achievement.

sentences.zh: 述春秋三傳，合成十卷。

translations.literal: He narrated the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, compiled into ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He narrated the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, compiled into ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 其所著詩頌賦誄章奏雜筆百餘篇，別有集。

translations.literal: What he composed—odes, hymns, rhapsodies, dirges, memorials, and miscellaneous pieces—number more than a hundred; there is a separate collection.
translations.idiomatic: His odes, hymns, rhapsodies, dirges, memorials, and miscellaneous pieces number more than a hundred; there is a separate collection.

sentences.zh: 彪雖與宋弁結管鮑之交，弁為大中正，與高祖私議，猶以寒地處之，殊不欲微相優假。

translations.literal: Though Biao formed with Song Bian the friendship of Guan and Bao, Bian as Grand Rectifier privately discussed with Gaozu and still placed him as from a cold district, quite unwilling to slightly favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Biao and Song Bian were close as Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya, Bian as Grand Rectifier still treated him as from a humble district and would not favor him.

sentences.zh: 彪亦知之，不以為恨。

translations.literal: Biao also knew it and did not take it as resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Biao knew it and did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 及弁卒，彪痛之無已，為之哀誄，備盡辛酸。

translations.literal: When Bian died, Biao grieved without end, composing for him a mourning dirge, fully exhausting bitterness.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian died, Biao grieved endlessly and composed a mourning dirge full of bitterness.

sentences.zh: 郭祚為吏部，彪為子志求官，祚仍以舊第處之。

translations.literal: Guo Zuo was Minister of Personnel; Biao sought office for his son Zhi; Zuo still placed him by old rank.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo was Minister of Personnel; Biao sought office for his son Zhi; Zuo still placed him by old rank.

sentences.zh: 彪以位經常伯，又兼尚書，謂祚應以貴遊拔之，深用忿怨，形於言色，時論以此譏祚。

translations.literal: Biao, his rank having passed regular minister and also concurrently Minister of Works, considered Zuo should raise him as noble kin; he deeply resented it, showing in words and countenance—the age's discussion thereby ridiculed Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, having passed regular minister and also been Minister of Works, thought Zuo should raise his son as noble kin; he resented it openly—the age ridiculed Zuo.

sentences.zh: 祚每曰：「爾與義和志交，豈能饒爾，而怨我乎？

translations.literal: Zuo often said: 'You and Yihe Zhi are friends—can he spare you, yet you resent me?
translations.idiomatic: Zuo often said: 'You and Yihe Zhi are friends—can he spare you, yet you resent me?'

sentences.zh: 」任城王澄與彪先亦不穆，及為雍州，彪詣澄為志求其府僚，澄釋然為啟，得列曹行參軍，時稱美之。

translations.literal: ' The Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, and Biao at first were not harmonious; when he became Inspector of Yongzhou, Biao visited Cheng to seek a post in his staff for Zhi; Cheng readily memorialized and obtained him as Acting Registrar in the Bureau—at the time praised.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng and Biao were at first not harmonious; when Cheng became inspector of Yongzhou, Biao sought a staff post for Zhi; Cheng memorialized and obtained Acting Registrar—praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 志，字鴻道，博學有才幹。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Hongdao, was broadly learned and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Hongdao, was broadly learned and talented.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，便能屬文。

translations.literal: At more than ten years he could already compose text.
translations.idiomatic: At more than ten he could already compose text.

sentences.zh: 彪甚奇之，謂崔鴻曰：「子宜與鴻道為『二鴻』於洛陽。

translations.literal: Biao greatly marveled at him and told Cui Hong: 'You and Hongdao should be the "Two Hongs" in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Biao marveled at him and told Cui Hong: 'You and Hongdao should be the Two Hongs in Luoyang.'

sentences.zh: 」鴻遂與志交款往來。

translations.literal: ' Hong thereupon and Zhi exchanged friendship warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Hong thereupon and Zhi became warm friends.

sentences.zh: 彪有女，幼而聰令，彪每奇之，教之書學，讀誦經傳。

translations.literal: Biao had a daughter, intelligent and clever from youth; Biao often marveled at her, teaching her book learning, reading and reciting the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had a daughter, clever from youth; he taught her the classics.

sentences.zh: 嘗竊謂所親曰：「此當興我家，卿曹容得其力。

translations.literal: He once secretly told those close: 'She will flourish our house; you may receive her strength.
translations.idiomatic: He once told intimates: 'She will flourish our house; you may receive her strength.'

sentences.zh: 」彪亡後，世宗聞其名，召為婕妤，以禮迎引。

translations.literal: ' After Biao died, Emperor Shizong heard her name and summoned her as Lady of Handsome Fairness, receiving her with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao died, Shizong heard her name and summoned her as a consort with ritual courtesy.

sentences.zh: 婕妤在宮，常教帝妹書，誦授經史。

translations.literal: The Lady in the palace often taught the emperor's sisters books, reciting and transmitting classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace she often taught the emperor's sisters, reciting classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 志後稍遷符璽郎中、徐州平東府司馬。

translations.literal: Zhi later was gradually transferred to Master of Seals and Tallies, Sima of Pingdong Headquarters in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi later became Master of Seals and Tallies and Sima of Pingdong Headquarters in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以軍功累轉後軍將軍、中散大夫、輔國將軍、永寧寺典作副將。

translations.literal: By military achievement he was repeatedly transferred to General of the Rear Army, Regular Grand Master, General Who Assists the State, and Deputy Director of Works at Yongning Temple.
translations.idiomatic: By military merit he rose to General of the Rear Army, Regular Grand Master, General Who Assists the State, and Deputy Director of Works at Yongning Temple.

sentences.zh: 始彪奇志及婕妤，特加器愛，公私坐集，必自稱詠，由是為高祖所責。

translations.literal: At first Biao marveled at Zhi and the Lady and especially favored them; at public and private gatherings he always praised them in verse—thereby he was reproved by Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: At first Biao favored Zhi and his daughter and always praised them in verse at gatherings—thereby reproved by Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 及彪亡後，婕妤果入掖庭，後宮咸師宗之。

translations.literal: After Biao died, the Lady indeed entered the rear palace; the inner palace all took her as teacher and model.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao died, the Lady entered the rear palace; all took her as teacher.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，為比丘尼，通習經義，法座講說，諸僧歎重之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong died, she became a Buddhist nun, thoroughly versed in scripture, lecturing from the dharma seat—the monks all sighed and honored her.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, she became a nun, versed in scripture, lecturing from the dharma seat—monks honored her.

sentences.zh: 志所在著績。

translations.literal: Wherever Zhi was, he left achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Zhi served, he left achievement.

sentences.zh: 桓叔興外叛，南荊荒毀，領軍元叉舉其才任撫導，擢為南荊州刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Shuxing rebelled externally, southern Jing was ruined; Army Supervisor Yuan Cha raised his talent for soothing guidance and promoted him to Inspector of Southern Jing, additionally General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Shuxing rebelled, southern Jing was ruined; Yuan Cha promoted him to Inspector of Southern Jing and General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 建義初，叛入蕭衍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he rebelled and entered Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he rebelled and went over to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 高道悅，字文欣，遼東新昌人也。

translations.idiomatic: An edict said: 'Daoyue is loyal and upright, establishes stern law, remonstrates with integrity—princes fear him; We praise his blunt sincerity—it shames not Ji An and Bao.'

translations.idiomatic: Also the entourage will bring wives—between boats men and women are mixed, inner and outer undivided.

translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingyuan Rui was nearing the capping age: in Beishi 40, Li Biao's biography, the character Lu appears above Rui.

sentences.zh: 按異姓王公例當書姓，這裏當脫「陸」字。

translations.literal: According to the rule that non-imperial-clan princes and dukes should write the surname, here the character 'Lu' is probably missing.
translations.idiomatic: Non-imperial princes should record the surname; Lu is probably missing here.

translations.idiomatic: Still lacking: various editions note que marginally, without ru.

translations.idiomatic: Cefu juan 529 Song edition has que ru; Ming edition juan 529

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6322〉

sentences.zh: 「闕」字亦旁注，「如」作「始」。

translations.literal: The character 'que' is also marginal; 'ru' is written as 'shi'.
translations.idiomatic: que is also marginal; ru is written as shi.

sentences.zh: 今據冊府宋本補正。

translations.literal: Now corrected according to the Cefu Song edition.
translations.idiomatic: Now corrected according to the Cefu Song edition.

sentences.zh: 未識儉素之易長 諸本「未」作「夫」，冊府同上卷頁作「未」。

translations.literal: Not knowing frugality's easy long growth: in various editions 'wei' is written as 'fu'; Cefu same juan page has 'wei'.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing frugality's easy growth: editions write wei as fu; Cefu same page has wei.

sentences.zh: 按作「夫」與上下文不貫，今據改。

translations.literal: Considering fu does not connect with context, now corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Fu does not fit context; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 時儉則加私之二 卷一一０食貨志「二」作「一」，通典卷一二輕重引李彪語此句作「儉則減私之十二糶之」。

translations.literal: In lean years add two-tenths to private: in juan 110 Food and Money treatise 'two' is written as 'one'; Tongdian juan 12 Light and Heavy citing Li Biao has this line as 'in lean years reduce private by one-tenth and sell grain'.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years add two-tenths: Food and Money treatise has two as one; Tongdian citing Li Biao has reduce by one-tenth and sell grain.

sentences.zh: 按常平本是政府為準備凶年而設立的，故當每逢凶年總是減價出售，似作「減」是。

translations.literal: Considering Ever-Normal Granaries were established by government to prepare for famine years, therefore in famine years price is always reduced in sale—seems 'reduce' is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal Granaries prepared for famine; in famine years grain was sold at reduced price—reduce seems correct.

sentences.zh: 但「加私之二」也可作加於收進價之二解。

translations.literal: But 'add two-tenths to private' can also be explained as adding two-tenths to the purchase price.
translations.idiomatic: But add two-tenths to private can also mean adding two-tenths to the purchase price.

sentences.zh: 故下云「歲凶則直給」，今不改。

translations.literal: Therefore below it says 'in famine years direct supply'—not changed now.
translations.idiomatic: Below it says in famine years direct supply—not changed now.

sentences.zh: 取州郡戶十分之一以為屯民 諸本及北史卷四０「民」作「人」，按食貨志載李彪語作「屯民」。

translations.literal: Take one-tenth of households in provinces and commanderies as colony people: in various editions and Beishi juan 40 'min' is written as 'ren'; Food and Money treatise records Li Biao's words as 'colony min'.
translations.idiomatic: One-tenth of households as colony people: editions and Beishi write min as ren; Food and Money treatise has colony min.

sentences.zh: 北史避唐諱「民」例改「人」，這裏本當同食貨志，亦唐人諱改，今改正。

translations.literal: Beishi avoids Tang taboo changing min to ren; here it should match Food and Money treatise, also Tang taboo change—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Beishi avoids Tang taboo min to ren; here should match Food and Money treatise—now corrected to min.

translations.idiomatic: 〈page 6324〉

sentences.zh: 按此用左傳莊十年曹劌論戰中「小大之獄，雖不能察，必以情」語。

translations.literal: Considering this uses Zuozhuan Zhuang 10 Cao Gui's discussion of battle: 'In small and great cases, though unable to examine, must by feeling.'
translations.idiomatic: This uses Zuozhuan, Cao Gui: in small and great cases, though unable to examine, must judge by feeling.

sentences.zh: 「二」字當是「以」之訛。

translations.literal: The character 'two' should be the error for 'yi'.
translations.idiomatic: Two should be the error for yi.

sentences.zh: 伏見朝臣丁父憂者 北史卷四０「父」作「大」。

translations.literal: I observe court ministers in father's mourning: Beishi juan 40 'father' is written as 'da'.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers in mourning: Beishi 40 writes father as da (great).

sentences.zh: 按下文，李彪主張「如有遭大父母、父母喪者皆聽終服」。

translations.literal: According to the text below, Li Biao advocated 'if encountering mourning for great-grandparents or parents, all permitted to complete mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: Below, Li Biao advocated mourning for great-grandparents or parents with full completion.

sentences.zh: 這裏也不可能專指「丁父憂」。

translations.literal: Here it also cannot specially mean 'ding father's mourning' only.
translations.idiomatic: Here it cannot mean only ding father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 「父」當是「大」之訛。

translations.literal: 'Father' should be the error for 'da'.
translations.idiomatic: Father should be the error for da.

translations.idiomatic: Truly as today: Cefu juan 658

translations.idiomatic: Below ru is yan; jin ri belongs to the next line—should be so.

translations.literal: Daoyue in youth was Secretariat student: in various editions 'sheng' is written as 'shi'; Beishi juan 40 Gao Daoyue zhuan has 'sheng'.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyue youth Secretariat student: editions write sheng as shi; Beishi 40 has sheng.

translations.idiomatic: Secretariat student appears repeatedly—shi is error—corrected to sheng.
